title: A Transferable Deprotonated Tyrosine Residue for Amber and CHARMM Force Fields
abstract: The deprotonated form of tyrosine gates proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) in ribonucleotide reductase and photosystem II, forms the anionic chromophore of fluorescent proteins, and acts as a general acid/base in enzymes, yet a validated, transferable tyrosinate residue for routine fixed-charge protein simulations in the major Amber and CHARMM force fields is lacking.

title: The Reverse Pourbaix Explorer: a condition-first screening tool of aqueous stability on the Materials Project
abstract: Aqueous stability is a critical constraint in the discovery of materials for electrocatalysis, corrosion-resistant systems, and electrochemical energy technologies. Conventional Pourbaix analysis follows a material-first workflow in which a predefined composition is evaluated across pH and electrochemical potential. Here, we introduce the Reverse Pourbaix Explorer, an interactive, condition-first screening application hosted on the Materials Project.

title: Hypothesis-driven multi-objective optimization of the Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction
abstract: Self-driving laboratories can optimize experiments, but whether they can reason scientifically about what to test remains unclear. Bayesian optimization (BO) provides uncertainty-aware search without explicit scientific interpretation, whereas language-model agents can formulate hypotheses but lack calibrated uncertainty. Here we introduce maLLaMar , which combines these capabilities in a physical self-driving laboratory. Using the Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction, we compare BO-only, agent-led and cooperative experiment selection under matched experimental budgets.

title: Hessian- and Property-Aware Learning of Analytic Bond-Order Potentials
Comparative Assessment of Degradation Pathways for Enzymatic Degradation of Polybutylene Terephthalate (PBT) and Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) and their Degradation Intermediates
abstract: Elucidating how polymer chemistry and substrate crystallinity collectively determine polyester degradability is a key to advancing enzymatic recycling as it enables predictive assessment of the degradation behavior of novel substrates and accelerates the development of efficient recycling strategies. Achieving this requires a systematic comparison across different polymer chemistries and crystallinity states. However, direct comparative studies remain scarce.

title: Gradient ascent pulse engineering (GRAPE)–a primer on quality functions and pulse shape penalties
abstract: Quantum optimal control is a versatile, powerful method to tailor quantum experiments. In NMR, numerical quantum optimal control algorithms such as the gradient ascent pulse engineering (GRAPE) algorithm have sparked many developments in pulse shaping, pushing the limits of pulse selectivity and robustness. To provide an overview of its core principles and the many expansions it has undergone ever since its introduction, the most common quality functions are benchmarked in their ability to guide the spin state transfer for facilitating excitation, inversion, and maximum quantum coherence.

title: From Individual Structure to Collective Topology: Cation Effects on the Hierarchical Organization of Interfacial Hydrogen Bond Networks
abstract: How electrolyte cations reshape the collective organization of interfacial water remains difficult to establish from local molecular descriptors. Here, we develop a graph-based hierarchical framework spanning molecular structure, network connectivity, and higher-order ring architecture, and apply it to molecular dynamics simulations of charged water/Pt(111) interfaces containing K + , Li + , and Ba 2+ . Molecular orientations respond primarily to surface charge, while molecular hydrogen bond statistics provide limited discrimination between Li + and Ba 2+ .

title: Improving 13C Benchtop Hyperpolarization with TOTAPOL as a Polarizing Agent
abstract: Dissolution dynamic nuclear polarization (dDNP) offers a solution to the naturally low sensitivity of NMR spectroscopy thanks to signal enhancements by several orders of magnitude. However, this methodology usually requires high magnetic fields and cryogenic temperatures (typ. > 3 T and < 4.2 K), which implies complex and expensive experimental setups, usually hosted in dedicated facilities. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in more affordable and cost-effective systems, and our group has developed an approach based on a simple and affordable benchtop DNP polarizer.

title: Ammonia combustion kinetic model optimization using elementary rate coefficient and global combustion data
abstract: Ammonia combustion kinetic models differ in key rate coefficients, and achieving consistent agreement with measurements across diverse conditions remains challenging. We optimize a detailed ammonia kinetic model derived from C3MechV4.0.1 for pure NH3, NH3/H2, and NH3/NO mixtures. The optimization uses direct rate determinations from 142 publications and 11,232 indirect combustion measurements from 113 publications, covering species concentrations, ignition delay times, laminar burning velocities, and extinction strain rates.

title: Development of a new isochromenylium-based derivatizing reagent for the analysis of α-amino acids and related compounds by LC-MS
abstract: A new pyrylium salt, 3,6,7-trimethoxyisochromenylium tetrafluoroborate (TriMIC), was developed for the derivatization of α-amino acids and other compounds with an NH2 group for use in LC-MS analysis. TriMIC was prepared using routine synthetic procedures from inexpensive raw materials. It has high reactivity, and derivatization of α-amino acids occurs under mild reaction conditions in an acetonitrile-methanol mixture. The efficiency of amino acid derivatization was evaluated using 10 amino acids.

title: Automating the Evaluation of Diffusion Coefficients from GITT Experiments using ”GITTcalc”
abstract: The galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) is a widely used method to evaluate the lithium diffusion coefficient in battery electrode materials. Here we introduce GITTcalc, an automatic analysis tool based on python for GITT experiments that extracts information about diffusion coefficients from raw data. It includes a graphical user interface (GUI) based on Tkinter and offers interoperability with OriginLab.

title: Motion in Stillness: An Open-Source Python Toolkit for Visualizing Time-Dependent Hydrogen Wavefunctions
abstract: Orbital shapes and nodes are core learning objectives in chemistry and physics. Many tools can render a wavefunc- tion’s phase as a color map. Yet rendering it is not teaching it: students often cannot explain what phase means, nor where Ψ’s time dependence lies. Since the density |Ψ|2 of a stationary state is constant, many infer Ψ is static. The opposite is true.

title: Ultrafast Non-Förster Energy Transfer in a DNA-Templated Cy3-Cy5 Assembly
abstract: Controlling electronic coupling between chromophores is central to the design of photonic materials, yet energy transfer at sub nanometer donor-acceptor separations, where the point-dipole Förster approximation becomes unreliable, remains difficult to probe experimentally. Here, we use a doublestranded DNA scaffold to position a Cy3 donor and a Cy5 acceptor within a few ångströms of each other and characterize their energy transfer using steady-state and femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, microsecond molecular dynamics and umbrella-sampling simulations, and TDDFT-based…

title: Gold(I)-Catalyzed Intramolecular Addition of Pyridines to Unactivated Alkenes: Synthesis of Indolizinium and Quinolinium Derivatives.
abstract: Nitrogen-containing heterocycles, such as indoliziniums and quinoliniums, are essential structural scaffolds in medicinal chemistry and include bioactive alkaloids of therapeutic interest. Herein, we report a regioselective gold(I)-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization enabling the addition of pyridine and quinoline motifs onto unactivated alkenes to form indolizinium and quinolinium derivatives in high yields, by using HFIP as the solvent and para-toluenesulfonic acid as an acidic additive.

title: A knowledge-aware, constraint-guaranteed decoder for cyclic peptides
abstract: Cyclic peptides reach a prized middle ground between small molecules and biologics: large enough to grip the flat protein–protein interfaces that defeat conventional drugs, yet sometimes lipophilic enough to be taken as a pill. Deep generative models have transformed small-molecule and protein design, but cyclic peptides are a harder frontier, with a design space of non-canonical residues, N-methylation, D-amino acids and macrocyclic rings that is far too large to search by hand.

title: From Small-Data Conductivity Prediction to Bayesian Optimization of Electrolyte Formulations with a Tabular Foundation Model
abstract: We evaluate whether a frozen tabular foundation model, TabPFN, can use limited measurements to predict conductivity and guide electrolyte formulation search without explicit transport equations or task-specific physics-constrained training. On the AMPERE conductivity dataset, 40 labeled context samples yield a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 5.56% on 60 held-out measurements, close to the 5.32% reported for the original physics-augmented AMPERE model and below the conventional regression baselines under locally matched conditions.

title: Order and entropy of lattices of unit vectors in d dimensions: label-free discovery of unusual local organization in simulated maintenance lattices and synthetic images
abstract: Averaged order parameters say how ordered a lattice of orientational states is, but not where its organization is unusual. We extend the local order and entropy quantities of the MyUncle maintenance-lattice model from the plane to unit vectors in d dimensions: the local disorder is one minus the length of the mean of the neighbors' unit vectors, and the information held in the local order follows from the von Mises-Fisher distribution; both equal MyUncle's at d = 2 (tested against the unmodified code).

title: Accelerating Quantum Chemistry with Emulated Double-Precision Matrix Multiplication on GPUs
abstract: The evaluation of exact exchange and the treatment of electron correlation remain major computational challenges in electronic-structure theory. Over the past decade, GPU computing has substantially accelerated these calculations, extending the scale and complexity of electronic-structure problems that can be addressed computationally. More recently, GPU architectures developed to meet the demands of artificial intelligence have introduced new opportunities for acceleration, with Tensor Cores providing reduced-precision arithmetic throughput far exceeding that of native double-precision…

title: Learning Rewards: Reconstructing Human Experimental Decisions from Scientific Data and Instrument Traces
abstract: For automated instrumentation, a central goal is to unlock the intrinsic operating bandwidth of instruments, with acquisition and control rates that can be several orders of magnitude faster than human decision and reaction times. Automated microscopy workflows now span fixed-policy protocols, reward-based optimization, and multistep agentic workflows. Each of these approaches depends on specifying either a rulebook, a reward, or a search over an increasingly large space of possible operations and observations.

title: Energetic-membrane discordance characterizes early Parkinson's disease with probable REM sleep behavior disorder despite preserved regional volumes
abstract: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) marks a clinically important Parkinson disease (PD) phenotype, but subgroup-specific biochemical findings may be detectable when regional-volume contrasts are small. We performed a quantitative secondary analysis of published group summaries from 26 patients with questionnaire-defined probable RBD, 46 patients without probable RBD, and 48 controls. Among four anatomical regions selected in the primary cohort, the largest combined energetic-positive and membrane-negative pattern was observed post hoc in the right basal ganglia.

title: Resistance Redistribution across Relaxation Times during CO2-to-CO Selectivity Oscillations
abstract: Selectivity oscillations between CO 2 reduction and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) limit stable operation of membrane electrode assemblies, yet cell voltage and total impedance cannot identify their origin. We combine operando galvanostatic impedance spectroscopy, frequency band integration of the distribution of relaxation times (DRT), and a membrane reference strip to track recurrent transitions in an Ag CO 2 -to-CO electrolyser. Over 70 h, the coefficients of variation of the total resistance and the 0.1-2 Hz band resistance were 6.6% and approximately 40%, respectively.

title: Site-Selective Photoredox Reactivity of Titanium-Oxo-Alkoxide Clusters in the Single Crystal Phase .
abstract: Titanium-oxo-alkoxide clusters with 7-17 Ti atoms are useful models of the surface of TiO 2 materials in alcoholic media as they contain a variety of different surface Ti-OR sites. These clusters undergo irreversible photoredox reactivity in the solid-state, which can be followed directly by X-ray crystallography upon irradiation of single cryst almounted on a diffractometer – noting that careful consideration of X-ray induced structural changes is required for accurate analysis.

title: Cation Identity and Framework Topology Govern CO2 Adsorption in FAU, MER, and RHO Zeolites
abstract: Preprint — Work in Progress. This manuscript presents ongoing research and has not undergone peer review. Additional solid-state NMR experiments and theoretical analyses are in progress, and the manuscript may be updated as further results become available.

title: An electrophilicity window reveals molecular allocation of protein-bound selenium
abstract: Selenium biology depends not only on total abundance but also on how selenium is allocated among molecular forms in proteins. Selenocysteine (Sec) is incorporated into selenoproteins, whereas selenomethionine (SeMet) can be retained more broadly throughout the proteome. Resolving these pools is limited by the incompatibility between complete protein hydrolysis and preservation of labile Sec.

title: Magnetic Dipole Response of Chiral Cavity–Molecule Systems from Real-Time Ab Initio Simulations
abstract: Conventional cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) fails to describe chiral environments due to its reliance on the electric-dipole approximation. We present a real-time QED time-dependent density functional theory (RT-QED-TDDFT) framework that overcomes this limitation through rigorous chiral light-matter Hamiltonians beyond the dipole approximation, enabling ab initio description of coupled electronphoton dynamics in chiral cavity environments.

title: Engineered NanoBiTs for multicomponent bioluminescence imaging
abstract: Bioluminescent enzymes are widely used as genetically encoded reporters in a variety of imaging contexts, but they are still limited in their capacity for multicomponent imaging. Though prior success has been found in development of new substrate-enzyme pairs, this process is time-consuming and requires complex chemistry. Here we introduce a new approach via engineering of NanoBiT, a split bioluminescent reporter. NanoBiT is comprised of an 11-amino-acid peptide (SmBiT) and a, 158 amino acid protein half (LgBiT).

title: Understanding the Trends and Origins of Electronic and Carrier-Transport Behaviour in CuSbCh2 (Ch = S, Se, Te) for Solar Energy Conversion
abstract: This study investigates the structural, electronic, and photoexcited carrier transport properties of CuSbCh2 (Ch = S, Se, Te) chalcogenides using first-principles calculations. We reveal that despite anisotropic lattice expansion, local coordination environments remain rigid, preserving the overall band-edge topology. Band gap narrowing arises from progressive conduction band minimum lowering due to enhanced Sb(p)-Ch(p) interactions.

title: Engineering Injectable Hydrogels from Lipoic Acid-Functionalized Polymer Micelles
Interpretable Prediction of Full UV-Vis Absorption Spectra of Organic Molecules in Solution
abstract: Accurate prediction of experimental UV–Vis absorption spectra is essential for understanding molecular electronic structures and guiding the design of organic optical materials. However, predicting full absorption spectra, particularly those containing multiple absorption bands and solvent-dependent spectral features, remains challenging. Here, we develop a hierarchical molecular graph attention network (HM-GAT) for predicting full UV–Vis absorption spectra of organic molecules in solution directly from two-dimensional molecular structures.

title: Symmetry Breaking in Argyrodite-Type Li6PS5X Solid Electrolytes and Its Implications for Thermodynamic Modeling
abstract: Argyrodite Li 6 PS 5 X (LPSX; X = Cl, Br, and I) solid electrolytes are highly promising for all-solid-state lithium batteries. While defect engineering in these materials is commonly investigated via computational methods, ideal high-symmetry crystal structures are typically selected as representative models without critically assessing their suitability as thermodynamic references.

title: Accelerating High-Pressure Simulations: Open-Source Implementation of the GOSTSHYP Model on GPUs
abstract: The Gaussians On Surface Tesserae Simulate HYdrostatic Pressure (GOSTSHYP) approach is a reliable method for calculating pressure-induced changes in molecular geometries, energies, electronic and spectroscopic properties, and reactivity. We present an open-source implementation of GOSTSHYP on Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) in the PySCF/GPU4PySCF program package, featuring energies and analytical nuclear gradients.

title: Predictive Life Cycle Assessment of Metal-Organic Frameworks
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are crystalline porous hybrid solids with a vast and diverse design space, making them promising candidates for applications such as gas storage and separation, water harvesting, biomedicine, sensing, and catalysis. However, environmental data on MOF synthesis and disposal are scarce because conventional life cycle assessments need to manually derive inventories from laboratory-scale synthesis protocols.

title: Enhancing proton-coupled electron transfer for electrochemical CO2 reduction to MeOH
abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction to methanol requires multiple proton-coupled electron-transfer (PCET) steps, but controlling proton delivery to catalytic intermediates remains challenging. Here, we regulate interfacial proton transfer by modifying cobalt phthalocyanine/carbon nanotube catalysts with protic ionic liquids (ILs). Methanol turnover exhibits a volcano-type dependence on 5 IL pKa, with maximum activity at pKa ~8-10.

title: Intramolecular protonolysis of platinum(II) methyl complexes: competing mechanisms for metal-ligand proton tautomerism
abstract: A series of neutral methylplatinum(II) complexes were synthesized bearing either pyridine or the protic 7- or 8-hydroxquinoline (7- or 8HQ) ligand, and an LX-type bidentate ligand. The 7HQ complexes undergo slow protonolysis to form CH 4 and µ 2 -quinolinolate dimers, while the 8HQ congeners form κ 2 -quinolinolate monomers. In both cases, protonolysis is dramatically faster when the supporting LX-type ligand is di- tert -butyl(benzyl)phosphine (P^C) instead of 2-phenylpyridine (N^C), consistent with the strong σ -donor properties of the phosphine.

title: Decyanation, Dioxygenation, and Oxidative Ring Contraction Catalyzed by the DUF4243 Oxidase OzmD Rely on Ferric Oxygen Activation
abstract: Domain of unknown function 4243 (DUF4243) family proteins are an emerging class of nonheme mononuclear iron enzymes characterized by a distinctive iron-binding motif comprised of four histidine (His) and one Nε-carboxylysine (Kcx) residue. Although predominantly found in fungi, OzmD is the only characterized bacterial member. OzmD catalyzes oxidative rearrangement of an aminopyridone ring into a 1,3-oxazine moiety with concomitant cyanide elimination in the final step of oxazinomycin biosynthesis.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Resistance Training Molecular Signatures Identify Pharmacodynamic Biomarker Candidates in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
abstract: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is characterized by progressive skeletal muscle loss for which validated pharmacodynamic biomarkers remain a critical unmet need. Biomarker discovery in DMD is fundamentally constrained by small patient cohorts and the ethical limitations of repeated muscle biopsy. Here we report that molecular signatures confirmed across seven independent exercise physiology datasets, spanning three species, four mass spectrometry platforms, and multiple independent laboratories, provide a high-confidence prior for evaluating directionally consistent findings in DMD muscle…

title: Type III polyketide synthases: from catalytic plasticity to predictive engineering
abstract: Covering: 1998 to 2026Type III polyketide synthases (PKSs) are homodimeric enzymes that catalyze starter-substrate loading, iterative condensation, and cyclization to produce diverse natural products, including chalcones, stilbenes, cannabinoid precursors, and curcuminoids. Despite their conserved catalytic architecture, type III PKSs exhibit remarkable plasticity in starter-substrate utilization, chain extension, and cyclization chemistry. This versatility makes them attractive but challenging targets for enzyme engineering.

title: SynthStrategy: Extracting and Formalizing Latent Strategic Insights from LLMs in Organic Chemistry
abstract: Modern computer-assisted synthesis planning (CASP) systems show promise at generating chemically valid reaction steps but struggle to incorporate strategic considerations such as convergent assembly, protecting-group minimization, and optimal ring-forming sequences. We introduce a methodology that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to distill synthetic knowledge into code. Our system analyzes synthesis routes and translates strategic principles into executable Python functions representing diverse strategic and tactical rules, such as strategic functional group interconversions, protecting strategies and ring construction features. We validate the use of LLM-as-a-judge in this domain, demonstrating their efficacy in evaluating synthesis-specific code generation. By formalizing this knowledge as verifiable code rather than simple heuristics, we create testable, interpretable representations of synthetic strategy. We release the complete codebase and the USPTO-ST data set─synthesis routes annotated with strategic tags. This framework unlocks a novel capability for CASP: natural language-based route retrieval, achieving 74.5% Top-3 accuracy on our benchmark. We further validate our library through temporal analysis of historical trends and chemically intuitive route clustering that offers more granular partitioning than common previous methods. This work bridges the tactical-strategic divide in CASP, enabling specification, search, and evaluation of routes by strategic criteria rather than structure alone.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Theory of large-bead AFM compression of pressurized rod-shaped bacteria
abstract: Motivated by our atomic force microscopy (AFM) experiments measuring turgor pressure in living bacteria, we develop a theoretical description of pressurized spherocylindrical cells compressed by spherical probes whose radius greatly exceeds the cell radius. In this global-loading regime, the mechanical response is governed primarily by cell geometry and turgor pressure, while the elastic properties of the cell envelope enter as higher-order corrections. The strong confinement imposed by the probe drives water efflux from the cytoplasm, thereby increasing the turgor pressure.

title: REVEAL: RNA Ensemble Validation and Exploration with AI-guided Landscapes
abstract: Capturing the sparsely populated but functionally important, excited states of RNA remains a central challenge for molecular simulation, because the underlying transitions are rare events that unbiased molecular dynamics cannot reach from a single starting structure. Here we introduce REVEAL (RNA Ensemble Validation and Exploration with AI-guided Landscapes), a workflow that couples generative secondary structure sampling, secondary structure conditioned tertiary structure prediction with trRosettaRNA2, unbiased molecular dynamics and Markov state modeling. Using only the sequence of the engineered HIV-1 TAR mutant, in which the excited state ES2 is the dominant conformation, we show that REVEAL captures the reversible ES2 to GS register shift from 6.8 s of aggregate unbiased sampling across 34 seeds, recovering both basins, the intermediate states, and correctly identifies ES2 as the dominant state, consistent with the design of the construct. In contrast, molecular dynamics seeded from the ES2-dominant HIV-1 TAR mutant NMR ensemble remains trapped in ES2 despite substantially longer aggregate simulation time, and sequence-only ensemble predictors (AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, ESMFold2, OpenFold3 and Protenix-v2) place every structure near the ground state and invert the experimentally observed population ordering. The information content of the seed ensemble, rather than the total simulation time, determines whether the transition is sampled. We further introduce ''population-weighted consensus score'' (PWCS) that ranks conformers by how representative they are of the equilibrium ensemble directly from the simulation data, without experimental restraints and independent of the choice of collective variables. PWCS identifies the dominant state even when low-dimensional representations fail to separate the states. Built entirely from open-source tools, REVEAL provides a transparent and extensible route to RNA conformational ensembles beyond the single-structure paradigm.

title: Where the magnet sits sets the sign of the scaling law: membrane-anchored versus intracellular magnetic actuation of cells
abstract: Magnetic nanoparticles apply mechanical force to cells in two incompatible geometries: anchored to the plasma membrane, where a rotating field twists a surface-bound cap, and internalized into lysosomes, where an assembled rod stirs the organelle lumen. They are treated as interchangeable, and the choice is made on synthetic convenience. They obey opposite design rules. Treated analytically at matched single-cell magnetic moment, the step-out frequency of an intracellular rod falls with assembly size while that of a membrane cap rises linearly; the scaling exponents have opposite sign and the curves cross at 184 particles and 4.04 Hz, inside the window in which published experiments operate. The cap tension resultant reduces to an identity in which cell radius cancels, leaving magnetic texture as the decisive design variable: a field-oriented cap reaches 2.69 mN m-1, the same particles with random easy axes reach 0.0033 mN m-1, and a superparamagnetic cap transmits no torque at all. The model reproduces four published measurements with no fitted parameters. One disagrees: our intralysosomal wall shear stress is 33 to 81 times below the published value while reproducing every structural feature of it. The model yields two zero-predictions that one experiment would falsify.

title: Advancing Clinical Trials and Precision Medicine in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Using Machine Learning-Based Trajectory Modeling and MRI Radiomics
abstract: Given heterogeneous progression of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), accurately characterizing individual disease trajectories is critical for effective clinical trials and therapeutic development. In this study, we applied machine learning (ML) approaches leveraging disease progression models and baseline magnetic resonance (MR)-derived radiomic features to quantify individual-level DMD progression trajectories and support quantitative characterization of disease progression.

title: Synergistic Interactions Enable Superior Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity in Compositionally Complex Nanocrystal–Nanosheet Hybrids
abstract: Thiospinel nanoparticles are promising catalytic materials due to their compositional tunability, electronic conductivity, and structural stability. While significant gains in catalysis have been made through material engineering, one continuously developing route is through the use of support materials to enhance performance. Here, we report a simple, scalable, low-temperature method to coproduce colloidal multimetal nanocrystals (<20 nm in diameter) and In2S3-based nanosheets (<1 nm thick), forming compositionally complex hybrid nanocrystal–nanosheet heterostructures in situ.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: From Sensor to Catalyst: Heme-Dependent Oxidative N -Demethylase Redefines Per-ARNT-Sim-Domain Chemistry via Amine Oxidase Mechanisms for Dimethylamine Demethylation, Vital N–C Bond Cleavage in Global N -Cycle
abstract: Microbial N–C bond cleavage plays a vital role in the nitrogen biogeochemical cycle. Heme-dependent oxidative N-demethylase (HODM), an enzyme identified within the Per-ARNT-Sim (PAS) domain family, challenges the traditional view of PAS domains as merely sensory modules by catalyzing the dimethylamine (DMA) demethylation to methylamine (MA) and formaldehyde via N–C bond dissociation. In this study, we employed density functional calculations to investigate the mechanistic landscape of the HODM reaction across multiple spin states.

title: Efficient Red Multi-Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters Based on DiKTa Core for Light-Emitting Electrochemical Cells
abstract: Multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters have demonstrated remarkable potential in optoelectronic applications; however, their utilization in light-emitting electrochemical cells (LECs), particularly efficient red-emitting devices, remains largely unexplored. Herein, a series of donor–acceptor MR-TADF emitters based on a DiKTa acceptor and diphenylamine-derived donors were developed to investigate the influence of donor strength on the photophysical properties and LEC performance.

title: Edible Crewed Spacecraft: A Multidisciplinary Feasibility Analysis of Dietary Redundancy in Human Spaceflight
abstract: Background: Long-duration crewed missions face irreducible uncertainty in resupply. Conventional redundancy relies on carrying extra emergency consumables, and that extra mass itself demands additional launch capacity, creating a recursive mass–payload constraint. This paper examines the edible design of non-critical spacecraft structures and consumable components, together with the pathways by which their material can be converted into food and nutrient resources after the mission.

title: FORGE: Flux-Orchestrated Reaction Generation Engine
abstract: The solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) that forms on a battery anode during the first cycles governs battery lifetime and safety, yet understanding how electrolyte chemistry gives rise to its molecular composition and mesoscale architecture remains a longstanding challenge. Electrochemical reaction networks (eCRNs) enumerated from firstprinciples thermodynamics and followed by kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) have emerged as a powerful, template-free route to predicting SEI products directly from electrolyte composition.

title: AnCore: A Six-Stage Structure-Based Virtual Screening Pipeline Integrating Two-Phase Redocking, Reciprocal Rank Fusion Consensus Scoring, and 300 K Langevin Dynamics Relaxation
abstract: Background. Structure-based virtual screening is routine in early drug discovery, but its desktop tools have not kept pace. Many rely on legacy Python or X11 toolkits that run poorly on modern macOS, handle one ligand at a time, and stop at a static docking score. Static scores ignore thermal and entropic effects. As a result, property-matched decoys with opportunistic hydrogen bonds can outrank true ligands. Methods. We built AnCore Scientific Studio, a native macOS workbench written in Rust/Tauri. It uses a WKWebView and 3Dmol.js interface and a six-stage Python engine.

title: Liquid Integrated Network as Candidate Substrate for Artificial Consciousness
abstract: Whether artificial intelligence (AI) system allows for generating machine consciousness has been a “grand challenge” which however must be answered in this day and age. Most contemporary AI is implemented on large scale solid-state electronic hardware, whereas biological consciousness is supported by much smaller sized space within a fluid-rich brain. Starting from this basic clue, here we propose to adopt five co-existing organizational criterions for searching candidate physical substrates of artificial consciousness (AC): Integration and differentiation, recurrence and history dependence…

title: GluA2 AMPA Receptor Binding Explains Simvastatin Neuroprotective Effects
abstract: Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to assess whether simvastatin can bind the agonist-binding site of the GluA2 AMPA receptor. Its deprotonated hydroxy acid form showed the most favorable MM/GBSA binding energy of the three forms studied and contacted residues that also anchor kainate, such as Arg485. These results suggest that simvastatin can occupy the agonist-binding site, which may contribute to its reported neuroprotective and antiepileptic effects.

title: Composable Chemical Formula Transformations with Invariant-Preserving Representations for Mass Spectrometry
abstract: Custom data-processing methods in high-resolution mass spectrometry require foundational software libraries for chemical formula representation and manipulation. However, existing libraries face a design tension between permitting unrestricted arithmetic and preserving invariants in public operations. This tension becomes particularly apparent when multi-step formula changes are expressed by chaining primitive arithmetic operations on a common formula type.

title: Chemoenergetics: Phase Geometry and Interference in Molecular Energy Organization
abstract: Every chemical transformation requires both a spatial rearrangement of atoms and a local convergence of energy. While structural chemistry and quantum mechanics explain how atomic connectivity governs the barrier of an isolated elementary step, and macroscopic thermodynamics balances the total energy of an Avogadro-scale ensemble, a foundational question separates the two: how do dispersed, discrete molecular energy inputs organize across space, time, and internal state space to drive a demanding chemical reaction at a single catalytic centre?

title: Out-of-Distribution Failures of HIP Molecular Hessian Checkpoints: Truncation, Cutoffs, and Errata
abstract: This work audits the released Hessian Interatomic Potential checkpoints (hip_v3.ckpt, hip_v3_cf.ckpt, and hesspred_v1.ckpt) on the 710-molecule PubChem size-generalization benchmark (N = 30–100 atoms), where the mean Eckart-projected eigenvalue error of hip_v3.ckpt on the 702 valid 3D geometries reaches 1.8234 eV/(Å²·amu) (CPU), more than 300 times the in-distribution HORM value (0.00545).

title: One Efflux Ratio, Two Validation Targets: Net Flux Asymmetry Is a Saturating Function of the P-Glycoprotein Pump Term
abstract: The bidirectional monolayer assay reports two apparent permeabilities. Their ratio, the efflux ratio (ER), is the endpoint against which computational models of Pglycoprotein efflux are scored. The same two numbers support two published readings of transporter activity: the net flux asymmetry as a fraction of the mean permeability, f = (ER − 1)/(ER + 1), and the pump term x = ER − 1. Which of the two a calculation should reproduce has not been examined. We show that f = x/(x + 2), a saturating map, so the two readings present different targets from identical data.

title: CueMol3: combining a web-based GUI with a native engine for
abstract: Interactive visualization of large biomolecular structures and molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories is essential for interpreting simulations and structural models, yet existing molecular viewers force a trade-off. Viewers built entirely with web technologies offer flexible graphical user interface (GUI) development but are limited by JavaScript performance, whereas native desktop viewers cannot take advantage of the web GUI ecosystem. Here we present CueMol3, a molecular viewer that combines an Electron- and React-based GUI with a C++ computational engine embedded as a Node.js native addon.

title: Process optimisation of fed-batch fermentation using online measurements alone
abstract: Advanced process control of penicillin fermentation holds the precursor phenylacetic acid, the criticalprocessparameteroftheprocess,ataset-point,butitdependsonadedicated measurement, an off-line assay or a Raman probe, whose model has to be maintained as the process changes. This study asked whether a fed-batch fermentation could be optimised from on-line measurements alone, without such a dedicated measurement, using the industrial-scale penicillinfermentationsimulatorIndPenSim.First,aPatchTransformerpredictedthe phenylaceticacidconcentrationfromsixteenon-linechannelswithanR2of0.989on…

title: Vibronic Ground-State Symmetry Beyond Scalar-Potential Reduction in a Benzene-Cation Model
abstract: We compare scalar and electronic-overlap reductions of a published three-state, two-coordinate benzene-cation model with fixed Jahn–Teller and pseudo-Jahn–Teller couplings. An analytic oscillator-tail bound and a residual-controlled finite-matrix certificate prove that its lowest orbital vibronic eigenvalue is exactly twofold and transforms as 𝐸 . By ground-state uniqueness, no adjustment of a finite real confining scalar potential with the ordinary single-valued nuclear kinetic operator can recover this multiplicity.

title: Single-isotherm non-identifiability of modified Dubinin–Astakhov parameters and the statement of system-level hydrogen-storage requirements in observable quantities
abstract: System-level targets for onboard hydrogen storage are routinely translated into required sorbent properties through the modified Dubinin–Astakhov (DA) isotherm. We quantify how much of that translation a single published isotherm can support. Two independent digitization routes, reconciled under a pre-registered rule with per-point uncertainties, recover eleven AX-21 excess isotherms (30–298K) from the literature; profile likelihoods under an explicit errors-in-pressure measurement model show that one 77K isotherm of ordinary published quality leaves the D–A parameter vector practically…

title: In Vitro Biological Characterization of Cystargolide-Based Fatty Acid Conjugates
abstract: Multiple Myeloma is a hematopoietic cancer characterized by a rapid build-up of monoclonal antibody proteins, which can result in cell stress and death. The degradation of this protein buildup is essential for cancer cell survival. Thus, Multiple Myeloma cancer cells depend heavily upon the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) to manage this protein stress and avoid cell death from the unfolded protein response. Proteasome inhibitors (PIs) are clinically approved and used in chemotherapy for Multiple Myeloma.

title: Evolution of Interfacial States Induced by Hydronium–Water Ordering on Au(111)
abstract: Structured interfacial water can substantially modify charge transfer at solid–liquid interfaces, yet direct spectroscopic evidence for how water ordering reshapes interfacial electronic states remains scarce. Herein, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), we identify parabolic interfacial states (IFSs) arising with the ordered water structures on Au(111), in striking contrast to the insulating nature of disordered water multilayers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Uncovering Features of ProteinMPNN with Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: Customization and modification of machine learning derived sequences can be achieved by understanding the mechanics behind state-of-the-art protein design models such as ProteinMPNN. Uninterpretability is hypothesized to be due largely to polysemanticity where neural networks store more features than they have dimensions. Here, we introduce sparse autoencoders (SAEs) into ProteinMPNN which expand its latent space and uncovers correlations between the activations in sparse dimensions and the presence of protein features such as secondary structure, residue volume, residue shape, disulfide bridges, and coordination to ligands. Additionally, we show that sparse activations can be manipulated to produce a variant of the short chain variable fragment Brolucizumab that is more thermostable than variants produced by traditional machine learning methods based on high temperature molecular dynamics simulations. Thus, SAEs provide both mechanistic understanding of protein design models and allow customizable manipulation of sequence prediction.

title: Interactive Learning with Low‑Performance Data for Accurate CO2 Reduction Catalyst Prediction
abstract: Emerging machine learning (ML) approaches offer transformative strategies to accelerate discovery for challenging objectives, such as developing practical catalysts through rational design. We propose an iterative learning framework and strategy that effectively enhances the predictive capability of the ML model, thereby accelerating catalyst development. By leveraging low-performance catalytic results, we have proven a practical, scalable framework for data-efficient catalyst development and for the broader application of ML methods in heterogeneous catalysis.

title: Uncovering Key Targets of Rhizoma Coptidis, Radix Scutellariae, and Cortex Phellodendri in the Treatment of Periodontitis through Integrated Network Pharmacology and Toxicology: A Study Leveraging Single-cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Data
abstract: IntroductionRhizoma Coptidis, Radix Scutellariae, and Cortex Phellodendri are used to treat periodontitis. This study integrated network pharmacology and network toxicology to elucidate their principal active compounds, key targets, and potential toxicity.MethodsUsing network pharmacology, differential expression analysis, and machine learning algorithms, key genes were identified from the intersection of genes associated with the active compounds of the three herbs and genes differentially expressed in periodontitis.
venue: Endocrine, metabolic & immune disorders drug targets

title: Inferring chromatin looping interactions from microscopy-based measurements: opportunities and pitfalls
abstract: Chromatin looping plays essential roles in several nuclear processes and live-cell microscopy has become a key method for studying how chromatin loops behave in time. Extracting dynamical parameters including looping probability, lifetime, and search time from live-imaging data requires inferring looping events from noisy 3D distance trajectories. By analyzing polymer simulation data with known ground truth, we show that with realistic localization precision, the common method of simple thresholding on 3D distance measurements can result in severe misestimation of looping probability, lifetime, and search time. We use simple statistical considerations to show that inference from simple thresholding becomes infeasible when localization error is comparable to the size of the interaction to be studied. Finally, we demonstrate how noise-aware methods can be used to estimate looping parameters more accurately in these regimes.

title: Catalytic domain-lipid interactions negatively regulate RhoA signaling by modulating conformational dynamics
abstract: RhoA belongs to the Ras superfamily of small GTPases, regulates cytoskeletal actin organization and cell motility, and is implicated in cancer metastasis and neurodegenerative diseases. It is predominantly anchored to the cytosolic side of the plasma membrane (PM) via its prenylated C-terminus, but little is known about its PM organization, dynamics, and lipid interactions. In this work, we used extensive atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and simulations-guided experiments to study the molecular details and functional consequences of RhoA membrane targeting, interactions and dynamics. We found that both GDP- and GTP-bound RhoA adopt a well-defined, stable membrane organization and binding mode irrespective of initial conditions and bilayer lipid composition. RhoA membrane organization is determined by hydrophobic interaction of the prenylated C-terminus with the membrane, and a previously unknown, critical role of electrostatic interactions between cationic residues on the G-domain and N-terminus with anionic lipids in the PM. N-terminal interactions are mediated by a polybasic patch including residues R5, K6, and K7, and substitution of these residues with Ala increased RhoA-mediated F-actin accumulation and effector activation in cells. MD simulations suggest that the triple mutant retains the global membrane organization of wild type RhoA but alters key protein-lipid interactions. Specifically, we observe a loss of cooperative lipid engagement involving the polybasic patch and Switch II residues with amine-bearing lipids, and a rerouting of intra-protein dynamic networks that primes Switch I for effector recognition. These results suggest that the membrane serves not just as a scaffold but also as an allosteric partner of RhoA to fine-tune intra-protein dynamics in a functionally relevant manner.

title: RNA Small-Molecule Binding-Site Prediction by Integrating RNA Language Models and Structural Geometry
abstract: RNAs are emerging as promising therapeutic targets, and small-molecule binding can modulate their structure and function, creating opportunities for therapeutic development. Accurate identification of RNA small-molecule binding sites is therefore important for understanding RNA-ligand interactions and facilitating RNA-targeted drug discovery. However, the structural complexity of RNA and the limited availability of experimentally characterized RNA-ligand complexes pose challenges for computational binding-site prediction.

title: Denaturation-sensitive BRET probes enable intracellular thermal shift measurements across diverse protein targets and biomolecular complexes
abstract: Thermal shift assays have revolutionized drug discovery, but can be limited in sensitivity and scalability. Combining the unique attributes of differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF) and cellular thermal shift (CETSA), we report the methodological framework for the bioluminescence resonance energy transfer shift assay (BRETSA). BRETSA utilizes denaturation sensitive BRET probes, in combination with luciferase-tagged target proteins, to track and longitudinally record thermal shift in living cells. Denaturation profiles were successfully measured for over 500 globular proteins, spanning 24 target families in diverse cellular compartments. Among these, target engagement was confirmed for over 200 proteins; including validated drug targets as well as understudied members of the kinase subfamily. Leveraging orthosteric, allosteric, and covalent ligands in potency studies, this method offers improved sensitivity and scalability compared to other thermal shift methods. We extend the utility of BRETSA to interrogate target engagement at biomolecular complexes and query cooperative binding for molecular glues and emerging tricomplex drug modalities.

title: A reproducible computational pipeline integrating network toxicology, nested machine learning, single-cell transcriptomics and molecular docking nominates cytoskeletal and BMP genes (ACTA2, BMP4, FLNA, FLNB) as bisphenol A–responsive markers of meningioma tissue
abstract: Background Bisphenol A (BPA) is a high-production-volume endocrine-disrupting chemical, and meningioma is a common hormone-sensitive intracranial tumour. A systematic, reproducible molecular map linking BPA-responsive genes to meningioma transcriptomes has been lacking. We therefore developed a fully computational pipeline that integrates multi-cohort transcriptomics, chemical–target databases, nested machine learning, single-cell localisation and molecular docking to prioritise candidate markers while treating all docking and classification outputs as computational evidence rather than…

title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.

title: Quantifying sample heating by ablation-plasma x-rays in laser-driven shock experiments
abstract: Sample preheat due to absorption of x-rays emitted by an ablation plasma has long been a source of uncertainty in laser-driven dynamic compression experiments. This unknown heating complicates interpretation of experiments designed to reach well-defined thermodynamic states, such as the principal Hugoniot, particularly because the pressure drive and sample heating occur simultaneously and are difficult to disentangle. Here, we quantify sample heating from x-rays using a unique experimental design in which the sample is heated prior to the arrival of the pressure wave. Using in situ x-ray diffraction, we relate lattice expansion to temperature within a 1-um-thick Au sample for commonly used 25-um and 75-um-thick Kapton-B (polyimide) ablators over a range of laser irradiances. Heating, sufficient to melt Au (Delta T ~ 1050 K), is observed for 25-um-thick polyimide ablators, which is significantly enhanced by the addition of a 0.2-um Al flash coating. In contrast, heating is strongly suppressed for 75-um-thick, non-Al-coated Kapton-B, with no measurable heating observed in 2.5-um-thick Ti or 1-um-thick Fe samples at laser irradiances up to 1.2 x 10^13 W/cm^2. .

title: TGen-SQD: Physics-Informed Transferable Configuration Generator for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization
abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) avoids iterative variational circuit optimization, but its accuracy and cost depend on selecting a compact determinant subspace that captures the ground state. Existing machine-learning selectors use task-specific physical cues and typically retrain for each Hamiltonian. We introduce TGen-SQD, a physics-informed generator jointly trained across multiple Hamiltonians. It learns from configuration-interaction-weighted data and uses orbital- and system-level descriptors to guide generation. After training, its weights remain frozen for inference on seen and zero-shot geometries. On a 20-qubit H10 chain, TGen-SQD achieves mean energy errors of 40.18 +/- 1.52 and 43.97 +/- 1.20 mHa on seen and unseen geometries, respectively, 12.7% and 11.7% lower than the state-of-the-art PIGen-SQD baseline under matched shot and proposal budgets.

title: Tunable Long-Range Magnetic Exchange in Adatom-Decorated Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Monolayers: An ab initio Embedding Model Study
abstract: Engineering magnetic interactions in two-dimensional materials offers a promising route toward programmable magnetic phases and reconfigurable spintronic functionalities. Here, we investigate magnetic adatoms on metallic monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) as a platform for tunable indirect exchange, focusing on Fe adatoms on monolayer TaS$_2$. In the intermediate-distance regime, DFT+U calculations reveal atomic-scale oscillations in the exchange coupling between two Fe adatoms and show that biaxial strain tunes the coupling. We develop a first-principles embedding model that reproduces the DFT-calculated pair exchange and establishes a substantial RKKY contribution to the exchange; controlled comparisons further identify RKKY-mediated coupling as the primary origin of the exchange's strain tunability. These results point to combining adatom arrangement with strain as a means of engineering reconfigurable magnetic interactions in metallic monolayer TMDs.

title: CupOFMoCA: Coupled Objective-Guided Discrete Flows for Molecular Conjugate Assembly
abstract: Molecular conjugates, including PROTACs and peptide-drug conjugates (PDCs), derive their function from the joint behavior of multiple coupled components, yet most generative approaches design these components independently and combine them only after generation. Such staged pipelines ignore cross-component dependencies and often produce conjugates that are chemically invalid, fall outside empirical conjugate distributions, or lose function upon assembly. In this work, we introduce Coupled Objective-Guided Discrete Flows for Molecular Conjugate Assembly (CupOFMoCA), a discrete generative method that enforces cross-component chemical constraints during conjugate generation. CupOFMoCA restricts guided updates to chemically feasible conjugate states and reweights local transitions using molecular design objectives. Across three PDC systems, coupled generation achieved 100% conjugation validity among valid peptides and increased valid yield over matched post-hoc filtering, with comparable predicted binding scores across the full valid sets. In three-seed evaluations of three PROTAC systems, CupOFMoCA achieved the highest assembly validity on two systems and generated more assembly-valid molecules per second than the evaluated baselines. We further evaluated the generated PROTACs with post-hoc DegradeMaster scoring and explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, supporting their predicted activity and conformational properties. Together, these results establish CupOFMoCA as an efficient generator of molecular conjugates, supporting therapeutic development via coordinated control of assembly and molecular properties.

title: Emerging synthetic biology toolkits to control gene expression and provide therapeutic avenues in cardiovascular disease
abstract: IntroductionSynthetic biology is an emerging field that integrates engineering principles, molecular innovations, interdisciplinary methodologies, and designer toolkits to create versatile and adaptable platforms for control, enhance, and reprogram signaling, phenotype, or function in biological systems and living organisms. Advances in mammalian synthetic biology have generated growing interest in its translational applications, including cardiovascular drug discovery and disease management.Areas coveredThis concise report highlights promising synthetic biology-inspired technologies that…

title: Design of colipids with controlled lateral distance of head group moieties for targeting strategies in the field of lipid-based nanoparticles
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles and liposomes are nanoparticle drug formulations which are firmly established in clinics. In order to expand their application and improve efficacy, surface modifications can be a key strategy, especially for cell specific targeting. Targeting can be achieved by integrating ligand functionalized lipids or lipidoids on the nanoparticle surface. In this case, not solely the targeting ligand itself, but also the structure of the whole targeting lipid/lipidoid can affect the interaction of the targeting ligand with the binding motive on cells.

title: Longevitomics as the Science of the Longevitome: Towards a Unified Systems Science of Healthy Longevity.
abstract: The twenty-first century has transformed longevity research through genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping and artificial intelligence. Yet healthy longevity remains difficult to explain because its determinants are commonly studied as separate molecular layers, mechanisms or biomarkers. Here, we introduce Longevitomics as an integrative systems framework for understanding, modeling and predicting healthy longevity and define the Longevitome inspired by the Latin expression vita longa (long life) as the dynamic architecture of…

title: Quantifying electro-osmotic flow in mutant MspA nanopores
abstract: Nanopores have emerged as a powerful tool for single-molecule sensing and sequencing. In a typical nanopore experiment, a charged analyte such as DNA is driven through the pore by an electrophoretic force generated by the applied electric field. This can be problematic, however, when analytes such as proteins carry mixed charges. An alternative driving force can be from electro-osmotic flow (EOF), the water flow that arises from an asymmetric migration of cations and anions through the nanopore. However, despite much recent interest, there is no straightforward experimental method to quantify EOF in nanopores. Here, we trap a dipolar peptide in an MspA nanopore, where studying its escape rate versus voltage allows us to extract the work done by the EOF in various MspA mutants and wildtype MspA compared to a M2-MspA reference. For the 30 amino acid model peptide, this yields values of ~5.6-16.7 kBT for the work done by the EOF at 80 mV. Finite-element simulations confirm the trends observed in the experiments. Charged mutations close to the nanopore's constriction site are found to produce the highest EOF. Our novel method provides a quantitative metric of the EOF in nanopores, opening up its study and broad use in future nanopore sequencing and sensing applications.

title: Pocket similarity guided selection of protein targets for systematic protein ligand dataset generation
abstract: The scarcity of large, diverse, and unbiased protein ligand binding datasets limits the performance of machine learning approaches in drug discovery, particularly for understudied proteins. The Target 2035 initiative aims to address this gap by generating open-access binding data for more than 2,000 human proteins, a goal whose value depends on maximizing the diversity of the selected targets.

title: Filament mechanics and turnover organize dynamic load bearing structures in a cellular-scale model of the actomyosin cortex
abstract: The actomyosin cortex controls cell shape and movement by generating and transmitting contractile forces. Its actin filament (AF) network adopts diverse spatial organizations, while spatially biased contractility drives cortical flow that transports components and reorganizes the network. However, how turnover and spatial redistribution organize and maintain tension-bearing structures in a dynamic steady state, and how localized contractility reorganizes them through flow, remain unclear. We developed a cellular-scale discrete model of the actomyosin cortex representing AFs, cross-linkers, and myosin minifilaments. Local surface stress was reconstructed from discrete-element internal forces based on continuum mechanics. We related cortical tension to component abundance, tensile deformation, AF orientation, turnover, and network connectivity, and compared different AF disassembly, relocation, and myosin-localization mechanisms. Simulations produced a heterogeneous, network-like distribution of local cortical tension. Tensile energy per element correlated more strongly with local tension than component abundance, with the strongest correlation for AFs. Highly stretched AFs preferentially occurred in high-tension regions and aligned with the first-principal-tension orientation, indicating anisotropic load-bearing pathways. Despite continuous component replacement and reorganization of local tension patterns, global AF-network connectivity and cell-scale cortical tension were maintained. The characteristic time of tension-pattern reorganization was closest to the persistence time of myosin, suggesting an association between myosin dynamics and rapid force redistribution. AF relocation to low-density regions replenished spatial gaps, whereas bending-dependent disassembly limited the accumulation of strongly deformed AFs. Direct myosin localization and AF accumulation produced comparable equatorward cortical flows but differed in the spatial organization of the tension-bearing network. Collectively, these results demonstrate that cellular-scale cortical tension is organized not only by component abundance but also by filament-scale mechanical loading, AF orientation, and network connectivity.

title: MoO x as an Oxidized Incorporation Modulates Nickel Sites for Efficient H2O2 Electrosynthesis at 200 mA cm–2
abstract: Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) enables on-site production, yet its practical application is hindered by the scarcity of catalysts that can simultaneously deliver high selectivity, activity, and stability at industrial current densities. Here, we report molybdenum incorporation into nickel oxide, where Mo is predominantly present as atomically dispersed, oxygen-coordinated Mo species (denoted as MoOx). The resulting MoOx–NiO catalyst features a hybrid crystalline–amorphous structure.

title: Relating Cu Phase Transitions to Selectivity Recovery During Pulsed CO2 Reduction on Gas Diffusion Electrodes
abstract: Pulsed electrochemical CO2 reduction on Cu catalysts represents a promising strategy to mitigate catalyst degradation and sustain high selectivity toward multicarbon (C2+) products. However, developing a detailed mechanistic understanding of the oxidative pulses remains challenging due to the inability to resolve the Cu oxidation state and the local electrolyte pH in the vicinity of the catalyst, especially inside a porous gas diffusion electrode.

title: Electrochemical food safety sensing via engineered MXene composites: from interfacial dynamics to intelligent devices
abstract: Two-dimensional MXenes have emerged as highly competitive scaffolds for electrochemical food safety sensing, however, their inherent tendency to restack and poor interfacial compatibility with delicate biomolecules frequently limit their analytical reliability in real-world sample matrices. To address these bottlenecks, this review critically evaluates recent advances in MXene-based electrochemical sensors, focusing on how multidimensional interface engineering, via the integration of carbon nanoscaffolds, inorganic catalytic nanomaterials, and functional polymers, fundamentally resolves…

title: Deepnude Forensics: Detection, Attribution, and Defense Against AI-Generated Intimate Image Abuse
abstract: The commoditization of open-weight generative image models has collapsed the technical and eco- nomic barriers to producing non-consensual intimate imagery (“deepnudes”) and, in its most severe form, synthetic Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM). Unlike photographic abuse material, synthetic content is unbounded in volume, detaches from any specific victim-identification signal, and sys- tematically defeats the perceptual-hash infrastructure (PhotoDNA, Project Arachnid, INTERPOL ICSE) on which global child-protection operations depend.

title: Conjugate Chiral Carbon Dots for Scalable Asymmetric Photocatalysis in Flow
abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as scalable, metal-free photocatalysts, but their use as conjugate organo-photocatalysts for enantioselective chemistry remains unexplored. Here, we covalently anchor a chiral imidazolidinone organocatalyst to amorphous, citric acid-derived CDs, giving a colloidal conjugate that acts as both photosensitizer and enantiodetermining component. This chiral CD material promotes the asymmetric radical α-alkylation of aldehydes in up to 84% yield and 93% e.e. Its semihomogeneous nature enables catalyst recovery by precipitation and reuse over five cycles with only minor loss in yield and e.e. The well-dispersed conjugate is also compatible with continuous photoflow, where Bayesian optimization in only 10 experiments enabled a gram-scale reaction in 80% yield and 91% e.e. This work establishes chiral conjugate CDs as a practical, recoverable platform for sustainable asymmetric photocatalysis.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Impacts of Environmental Nickel and Chromium Exposure on the Blood Proteome of House Sparrows (Passer domesticus) in New Caledonia
abstract: New Caledonia holds some of the world's largest ultramafic mineral deposits, and nickel (Ni) smelting operations have created a gradient of Ni and chromium (Cr) contamination across the archipelago. Molecular impacts of Ni and Cr toxicity on wildlife remain largely unexplored. Here, we used the house sparrow (Passer domesticus) as a sentinel species to characterise the blood proteomic response to Ni and Cr exposure near the Doniambo smelter in Noumea. Blood was collected from 52 free-living sparrows across 18 sites classified by soil metal concentration. Plasma and blood cell pellet fractions were analysed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Plasma proteomics identified histidine-rich glycoprotein (HRG) as the most prominent responder, with approximately 2.1-fold elevation in exposed relative to low-exposure birds. HRG contains a conserved histidine-rich region that binds cations including divalent nickel, and paired plasma-liver analysis confirmed hepatic-driven synthesis. Blood cell pellet proteomics revealed that Ni-Cr co-exposure predominantly disrupts the nuclear compartment: histone depletion indicated chromatin collapse, NUP153 dysregulation impaired nuclear pore function, and VRK1/TRIP13 upregulation suggested DNA damage response activation coupled with mitotic checkpoint override. Concurrent RNA processing collapse (DDX17, DHX15, RBMX, ALYREF) and changes in telomere-associated proteins (TERF2IP, hnRNPA1 and VRK1) implicated disrupted genome maintenance. These findings identify HRG as a candidate plasma biomarker of Ni-Cr exposure and reveal a coordinated nuclear toxicity signature linking heavy metal contamination to DNA damage and epigenetic disruption in a free-living vertebrate.

title: Zeolite-Confined Triatomic Cu Oxides at Silanol Nests as Hydrogen Transport Channels for H2 Production from Methanol Steam Reforming
abstract: Cu-based catalysts offer high methanol steam reforming (MSR) activity but are limited by unstable Cu+–Cu0 interconversions due to the redox and sintering labilities of Cu. Herein, we developed a universal amino-functionalized “gripper” strategy for firmly and precisely anchoring atomically dispersed metals (e.g., Cu, Co, Ni) within Beta-zeolite. Triatomic Cu oxide (Cu3Ox) sites lower the methanol dehydrogenation activation barrier, and the synergistic interplay with adjacent OH groups from silanol nests accelerates H2 evolution and the MSR reaction.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: MicroRNAs in aflatoxin B1-associated hepatocellular carcinogenesis: a scoping review of molecular networks, multiomics evidence, machine learning and translational potentials
abstract: BackgroundAflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a foodborne hepatocarcinogen, but it remains unclear whether microRNA dysregulation reflects AFB1-associated hepatocarcinogenesis or general hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) biology. This scoping review mapped evidence linking AFB1 exposure, microRNA regulation, molecular mechanisms, multiomics, computational modelling, and machine learning approaches to HCC diagnostics, prognostics, and therapeutics.MethodsPeer-reviewed studies published from 2016 to 2026 were identified through Scopus, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science, supplemented by citation searching, and screened using PRISMA ScR-aligned criteria. The final corpus comprised 104 unique studies classified by AFB1 attribution strength and evidence type across five strata spanning direct human AFB1 HCC microRNA evidence to general HCC contextual evidence.ResultsExperimental mechanistic studies predominated, whereas only one study directly combined measured AFB1 exposure, HCC, and microRNA assessment in humans. The study enrolled 366 HCC cases and 662 controls; circulating miR-4651 provided the strongest exposure-anchored clinical signal, discriminating AFB1-positive HCC with an area under the curve of 0.85, 78.1% sensitivity, and 92.1% specificity. Other studies evaluated exposure-responsive hepatotoxicity, experimental malignant transformation, or rat hepatocarcinogenesis, which cannot be considered interchangeable endpoints. Functionally investigated injury candidates included miR-1679 and miR-124a-3p. Multiomics findings implicated DNA damage, methylation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, inflammation, and metabolic dysregulation, although pathway overlap was heterogeneous and independent functional confirmation was limited. Computational and machine learning studies have expanded network and feature prioritisation, but they have often relied on inferred exposure and limited external validation.ConclusionDirect human evidence remains scarce, and candidate microRNAs occupy different validation stages. Biological plausibility does not establish clinical readiness; multicentre exposure-anchored validation, harmonised assays and prospective evaluation are required.

title: Differential properties of gp120 from HIV-1 group M subtypes A and B
abstract: HIV-1 group M subtypes A and B differ substantially in their gp120 sequence. To determine whether these differences contribute to subtype-specific complications, particularly pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), rats were injected with gp120 from subtype A or B. Pulmonary artery (PA) remodeling was assessed after four weeks using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining and the Vessel Morphometry Analysis tool by Autona (autona.org). Subtype A gp120 potently increased PA wall thickness and right ventricular hypertrophy.
