title: Durability Assessment of α-MnO2 Nanorods for Alkaline ORR under Application-Relevant Conditions
abstract: This study investigates the durability of α-MnO2, one of the most cost-effective catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in alkaline media. A comprehensive set of various characterization techniques, including identical location transmission electron microscopy (IL-TEM), differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), rotating ring-disk electrode (RRDE), and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) coupled to both flow cell and gas diffusion electrode (GDE) half-cell, was employed. In addition, accelerated stress test (AST) measurements in the GDE half-cell followed by post mortem X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and TEM analysis were performed. Three electrolyte and temperature combinations ranging from standard lab conditions to application-relevant conditions were systematically investigated. The results reveal that Mn dissolution occurs under oxygen-free conditions due to oxidation-state transitions of the catalyst, whereas under oxygen, it is further accelerated by degradation processes associated with peroxide formation as a byproduct of the ORR, particularly at higher ORR overpotentials. Both increasing KOH concentration and temperature significantly enhance Mn dissolution due to accelerated Mn reduction and dissolution kinetics. Despite the increased dissolution, the condition of 4.0 M KOH at 25 °C exhibits the highest ORR activity after 5000 AST cycles. This apparent discrepancy is attributed to surface roughening of the catalyst, leading to an increased electrochemically active surface area. Overall, the results demonstrate that α-MnO2 exhibits promising initial ORR activity but undergoes substantial Mn dissolution under operating conditions. These findings provide mitigation strategies to limit catalyst degradation and improve operational durability.

title: Nonlinear waveguide polaritons for long-distance propagation of spins at room temperature
abstract: In spintronics, the spin of particles is used to transfer information but the propagation distances are short, whereas photons carry spin further but lack the nonlinear interactions necessary for logic gates. Now, polariton waveguides built from transition metal dichalcogenides enable spin propagation of up to 100 μm at room temperature and maintain large polariton nonlinearities.

title: Where AI can aid chemistry research and where reliability falls short
abstract: Researchers from the Skoltech AI Center, together with colleagues from the Zelinsky Institute of Organic Chemistry of the Russian Academy of Sciences, ITMO University and other institutions, have published a paper in Chemical Society Reviews that examines where AI produces measurable value in a chemical research workflow, how to assess its reliability and why a strong benchmark result does not necessarily translate into laboratory performance.

title: Depth determination from core-loss 4D-STEM
abstract: Moving beyond specimen-projected micrographs in scanning transmission electron microscopy to determine the three-dimensional distribution of dopants is of vital importance for materials characterization and development. We present an approach for dopant depth determination using momentum-resolved core-loss four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy data. Within the Born approximation, Fourier transformation over probe position reveals fringes whose frequency encodes the dopant's distance from the focal plane. Two principal challenges arise in extending this approach to realistic experimental conditions. First, dynamical scattering degrades fringe contrast which can be partially mitigated by acquiring off major zone axes. Second, because core-loss doses are punishing, we use a Bayesian framework which, in simulation, achieves nanometre to sub-nanometre depth precision from only 100 to 1000 core-loss counts, depending on the signal-to-background.

title: Reducing TLS Losses in Superconducting Circuits Using Solid Neon
abstract: Two level systems (TLSs) are a major source of loss in superconducting devices, limiting the performance of qubits, detectors, and resonators. These defects arise from a range of sources, including surface oxides, crystal defects, as well as fabrication residues which are often difficult to remove. Using NbTiN coplanar waveguide resonators, we show that depositing and subsequently removing a solid neon film can significantly improve device performance. Analysis of the temperature and power dependence indicates that this enhancement arises from reduced TLS dissipation, which we attribute to the redistribution and removal of surface contaminants during neon deposition and evaporation. Atomic force microscopy images of contaminated hexagonal boron nitride flakes before and after neon exposure show that neon treatment can redistribute and remove surface residues. These results demonstrate a simple, non-destructive approach for mitigating TLS losses in superconducting devices and other sensitive materials that cannot withstand aggressive cleaning processes.

title: Defective $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$ from first principles
abstract: $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$ is a two-dimensional van der Waals material with promising applications involving ferroelectricity. However, the presence of native defects can significantly influence its structural and electronic properties. In this work, we employ density functional theory with a state-of-the-art meta-generalized gradient approximation (meta-GGA) exchange-correlation functional to investigate the electronic structure of bulk $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$ and the formation of neutral point defects, including vacancies and antisites, under Se-rich and In-rich growth conditions. Our calculations reproduce the experimental structural parameters of the pristine material and reveal that the Se vacancy in the middle layer exhibits an unexpectedly low formation energy under both chemical environments. Structural analysis shows that the neighboring tetrahedrally coordinated In atom undergoes a substantial local relaxation along the three-fold axis, which preserves its $C_{3v}$ site symmetry even as its coordination is reduced from four to three, providing a microscopic explanation for the remarkable stability of this defect.

title: Science Prediction Universe
abstract: Humanity has long sought to explain natural phenomena. Reliable prediction of experimental outcomes is a central test of our understanding of the processes that produce them. If artificial general intelligence (AGI) is to surpass human scientific capabilities, it must also predict experimental outcomes more reliably than humans. Such capabilities could accelerate scientific discovery across disciplines, help address humanity's most pressing challenges, and improve human well-being. We introduce Science Prediction Universe (SPU), a benchmark of hidden experimental outcomes with 100 public verified tasks from chemistry, materials science, biology and medicine, and 16 private tasks from unpublished wet-lab experiments. Given an experimental setup and candidate conditions, an agent works with any resources it needs to rank the candidates by a measured outcome. We evaluate thirteen agent configurations spanning twelve frontier models across two harnesses (Codex and Claude Code). Current agents remain far from saturating wet-lab outcome prediction, with substantial performance disparities across models: on the public benchmark, configurations separate into two distinct tiers, with task-adjusted Spearman correlations ranging from 0.227 for the lowest-performing configuration to 0.478 for the best. Analysis of 1,155 scored public trajectories (227,103 tool calls) suggests that the bottleneck lies in scientific judgment rather than tool execution: agents rely on shared monotone priors, agreeing far more with one another than with experimental reality (0.52 vs. 0.33), and frequently compute trivial physical or chemical proxies that do not influence the final outcome.

title: Self-assembly versatility of N-acyl amino acids
abstract: N -acyl amino acids (NAAAs) are prebiotically plausible amphiphiles that can emerge from simple fatty acids and amino acids under abiotic conditions. As hybrid molecules combining two fundamental classes of prebiotic building blocks, NAAAs may have contributed to the emergence of structurally and functionally diverse molecular assemblies during early chemical evolution. However, how amino acid side chains influence their self-assembly behavior remains poorly understood.

title: Conformationally driven negative chemotaxis in synthetic vesicles
abstract: Chemotaxis—directed movement in response to environmental cues—is fundamental to biological systems but remains rare in artificial systems, where it typically relies on complex catalytic pathways or intricate adaptive designs. The molecular mechanisms underlying artificial chemotaxis are still scarce and poorly understood, posing challenges for the rational design of advanced artificial chemotactic systems. Here we present a minimal polymeric system that achieves negative chemotaxis through intrinsic conformational dynamics, enabling mechanical transduction and directional movement without the need for catalysis or external energy input. Our study uncovers a previously unrecognized molecular mechanism in which hydrophobic membrane domains dynamically reconfigure in response to chemical signals, triggering a cascade of events, from conformational rearrangements to interfacial tension alterations that generate self-sustained motile behaviour. By elucidating the interplay between membrane dynamics, interfacial forces and directional transport, our findings advance the molecular understanding of synthetic systems that emulate cytoskeletal remodelling in biological motility and establish a versatile framework for engineering functional artificial protocells with life-like behaviours.

title: Plasma ATR-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning for early classification of response to neoadjuvant endocrine therapy: exploratory results from the ANNE trial
abstract: PurposeNeoadjuvant endocrine therapy (NET) is an effective treatment strategy for luminal breast cancer, but early identification of responders remains challenging. ATR-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning may provide a low-cost, minimally invasive liquid biopsy approach for capturing biochemical information from plasma.MethodsThis exploratory study was embedded within the ANNE trial, a prospective single-arm phase II study evaluating neoadjuvant anastrozole in stage II-III luminal breast cancer.

title: Beyond Sequence and Structure: Pretraining PLMs on Continuous Biophysical Fields
abstract: We introduce the Biophysical Transformer, a protein language model that adds continuous biophysical fields as a third pretraining signal beside sequence and structure. A Poisson-Boltzmann solver computes the electrostatic potential around each three-residue token, and the model learns to predict it from sequence alone. A rotationally invariant spherical-harmonic descriptor serves as the loss target, eliminating the need for frame alignment during training and for coordinates at inference. Against a matched, one-flag control on the FLIP Meltome thermostability benchmark, the field objective raises Spearman correlation on every trained head of both human splits.The gain on human survives residualizing dipeptide composition under two architecturally different readouts and survives removing the test proteins that overlap the pretraining corpus. No effect survives on the organism-mixed split. At 1.1M parameters, both the Biophysical Transformer and its sequence-only control exceed FLIP's one-hot CNN and untrained-ESM baselines on every split. All results rest on a single pretraining run per arm,and the current design does not separate field content from generic regularization.

title: Structural relationships between the SLC12 cotransporter C-terminal domain, universal stress proteins and adenylating enzymes
abstract: Several SLC12 cotransporters bind ATP in a cytoplasmic C-terminal domain (CTD). We analysed 16,192 CTD-containing SLC12 sequences and compared 42,845 representative structures to examine the relationship between this nucleotide site, universal stress proteins (USPs) and adenylating enzymes. In phosphorylated NKCC1, D891 and D927 lie near the ATP phosphate chain, while R801 and K889 form a basic phosphate-binding clamp. NKCC1 retains this arrangement, whereas KCC paralogs replace or lose several corresponding groups. In structural comparisons with USP and adenylating-enzyme references, both CTD lobes score between universal stress proteins and EC-annotated domains, and the two lobes form separate lineages that include bacterial transporters. Lobe-specific and nucleotide-frame comparisons place ATP in the corresponding structural region used for -phosphate chemistry by catalytic members of this fold. Published work on UspG provides a precedent for protein-bound AMP in a natural USP. In the examined SLC12 structures and USP models, candidate protein hydroxyls lack an in-line geometry for attack at ATP P. Protein adenylation would require a change in protein or nucleotide geometry, or a different acceptor. These results define a structural basis for testing conditional protein adenylation at SLC12 nucleotide sites. The required evidence is a covalent protein-AMP adduct, identification of its acceptor and measurement of the expected pyrophosphate coproduct, with soluble nucleotide analysis to distinguish accompanying ATP reactions.

title: Binding mechanisms of therapeutic antibodies to human claudin-18.2
abstract: Claudin-18.2 (CLDN18.2) is a tight junction component with highly restricted expression in the paracellular space of nonmalignant gastric epithelial cells. It becomes accessible on tumor cell surface during malignant transformation, making CLDN18.2 an attractive target for targeted therapies against gastric cancer. Recently, zolbetuximab has become the first FDA-approved monoclonal antibody that targets CLDN18.2 in advanced gastric cancer, and others like osemitamab have entered phase 3 clinical trials. However, the high-resolution structure of CLDN18.2 is lacking, and how CLDN18.2 is recognized by therapeutic antibodies remains undefined. Here, we report cryo-EM structures of human claudin-18.2 (hCLDN18.2) in complex with the Fab fragments of zolbetuximab and osemitamab, revealing the structure of hCLDN18.2 and its binding mechanism to the therapeutic antibodies. Further analyses reveal that three residues in the first extracellular loop of hCLDN18.2 that are different from human claudin-18.1 (hCLDN18.1) play a critical role in antibody binding. Our data elucidate the structural basis for selective binding of therapeutic antibodies to hCLDN18.2, which should aid rational design of next-generation immunotherapies targeting hCLDN18.2.

title: An auditable harness for biomolecular dynamics simulations by AI agents
abstract: AI agents now generate biological hypotheses faster than they can be tested. Hypotheses stated at the atomic level can be examined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. For new questions without a reference, trust in an agent-run simulation rests on a tool-written process record, not the agent's account. Existing MD agents leave this record to the language model. Here we present MDClaw, a harness whose validating tools and directed acyclic graph (DAG) check stages before execution and record every simulation stage. On MDDataBench, which grades outputs against deposited simulations, four open-weight models with MDClaw passed all three runs on 81-100% of 31 test systems. The DAG complements this outcome check. An ablation without the DAG revealed 11 successful runs that had skipped minimization or equilibration, or simulated a different structure. MDClaw carried questions from human and AI scientists through simulation to trajectories traceable to their inputs and settings.

title: Affordable 96-parallel SPPS: hardware and software add-on for automated liquid handling platforms
abstract: ParSynt-P is a hardware and software add-on that converts a liquid-handling robot already available in a proteomics laboratory (Tecan Freedom EVO) into a parallel plate-format peptide synthesizer for generating libraries of candidate peptide standards for targeted blood plasma proteomics. The manifold is milled from polytetrafluoroethylene and has ports for an inert gas and a vacuum line; a standard commercially available 96-well filtration plate is secured to it with an airtight seal. The software layer generates robot worklists from a table of peptide sequences and controls switching of the N?/vacuum lines, including pulsed gas mixing. The system performs up to 96 syntheses per run, and coupling of one residue takes 94 min. Workability of this 96-well format was verified on three fully loaded plates. The uniformity of synthesis conversion across the plate was measured quantitatively using a characterized NAT/SIL standard pair. The add-on cost $351, while the synthesis cost is $0.23 per coupling and $1.14 per milligram of crude product, an order of magnitude below the market price of custom synthesis.

title: New organic iron-sulfur framework boosts photosynthesis and carbon fixation
abstract: Iron-sulfur clusters are ancient protein cofactors that are essential for electron transport, enzyme catalysis and photosynthesis. However, their sensitivity to oxygen and inherent instability have long hindered their practical application.

title: Oxygen Vacancy Distribution as a Structural Switch for Oxygen Cycling: A Local Oxygen Chemical Potential Descriptor for Methane Oxidative Coupling on SrTiO3
abstract: Oxygen species evolution is central to the catalytic performance of oxidative coupling of methane (OCM), yet understanding and controlling this evolution remains a major challenge. SrTiO3 is a promising OCM catalyst due to its high C2 selectivity and stability but suffers from low activity. Here, DFT calculations combined with kMC simulations were employed to investigate facet-dependent oxygen species cycling on SrTiO3. Our findings reveal that SrTiO3(100)-Ti is the most favorable facet, sustaining a regenerable oxygen cycle (“O2− → OV → O22− → Ti-OH → O2−”).

title: Anisotropy driven critical phenomena in a van der Waals ferromagnet
abstract: We report a detailed investigation into the field-dependent critical behavior of the van der Waals ferromagnet $\mathrm{Fe_3GeTe_2}$ to elucidate how applied magnetic fields ($B$), strong magnetocrystalline anisotropy, and emerging other energy scales modulate its critical behavior. Utilizing the recently developed method, viz., the average of normalized slope (ANS), for analysis of critical behavior, we evaluate the critical exponents ($β$, $γ$, and $δ$) across distinct field windows up to $\rm{7\,T}$. For $B$ applied along the crystal's easy axis ($B\parallel c$), the system exhibits long-range interactions dominated by competing double-exchange and itinerant Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) mechanisms, which is systematically suppressed with increasing $B$ to converge toward the long-range 3D Ising universality class ($β\sim0.330$, $γ\sim1.00$). Conversely, under an in-plane hard-axis configuration ($B\perp c$), the critical behavior study exhibits a sub-unity regime ($γ<1$) across the measured range of $B$. This behavior is attributed to the intense competitive interplay between the external Zeeman energy and strong out-of-plane magnetocrystalline anisotropy. Our findings demonstrate that critical behavior in nontrivial van der Waals magnets is fundamentally modulated by the orientation of $B$ and the strength of magnetocrystalline anisotropy, demonstrating the necessity of $B$-dependent critical behavior investigation over conventional frameworks.

title: TabOmics: A Small, Open Tabular Foundation Model for Wide Omics Data
abstract: Omics studies often produce tables with thousands to tens of thousands of molecular features and few samples. Tabular foundation models use diverse strategies to predict labels for such tables, with some relying on in-context learning, while approaches to wide tables may involve subsampling, grouping, or compressing features. We present TabOmics, a small, open family of tabular foundation models with 7.3M parameters, pretrained exclusively on synthetic tables. TabOmics processes all features retained after preprocessing jointly and derives predictions, attention-derived feature-importance scores, and test sample embeddings from the same forward pass. On 46 classification tasks from three benchmarks of high-dimensional, low-sample-size tables, TabOmics v2.5 with eight ensemble members achieves the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) among the evaluated models (0.943), outperforming TabPFN-3.5 with eight members on 32 tasks despite having about 30 times fewer parameters. With a single member, TabOmics v2.5 reaches a mean AUROC of 0.941, versus 0.942 for TabPFN-3.5 with eight members, with no significant paired difference under the reported task-level analysis. On synthetic tables, its feature-importance scores achieve feature recovery similar to that of TabPFN-Wide, and its predictions remain above chance at 30,000 features. On breast cancer tasks, the top ranked genes include PAM50 genes, which define the subtype labels, indicating concordance with the label definition rather than independent biological validation. The code, model weights, training recipes, and experimental artifacts are publicly available.

title: Directed Domain Wall Motion by Radio-Frequency Currents
abstract: Magnetic domain walls (DWs) are central to emerging spintronic technologies for memory, logic and neuromorphic computing, where their controlled displacement is a key functionality. While current-induced DW motion driven by spin-orbit torques is well established under direct currents, it remains unclear how radio-frequency (RF) currents couple to DWs and whether they can generate directed motion under a symmetric periodic drive. Here we show that RF currents drive DW oscillations, which can be rectified into directed motion through symmetry breaking. Using time-resolved and static magneto-optical Kerr microscopy, we demonstrate that RF spin-orbit torques efficiently excite low-frequency DW oscillations well below the ferromagnetic resonance frequency. Whereas these oscillations remain symmetric in the absence of perturbations, symmetry breaking by a transverse magnetic field produces self-propulsion, while symmetry breaking by an initial current pulse gives rise to sustained DW motion. We further show that in initially uniform magnetic states, RF-driven expansion of a pulse-generated edge domain ultimately results in efficient RF-assisted magnetic switching. Together, these results establish a general framework for understanding how RF-driven DW oscillations are rectified into directed motion, providing new opportunities for their high-frequency control.

title: Charge Transfer Engineering in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Red Visible Light-Driven Coenzyme Interconversion
abstract: Precise photocatalytic modulation of the NAD+/NADH redox balance is critical for advancing both biocatalytic cascade reactions and photodynamic therapy, yet this goal remains elusive due to the scarcity of efficient, broad-spectrum photocatalysts with orthogonal redox regulation capabilities. Herein, we report a bifunctional covalent organic framework-polyoxometalate (COF-POM) composite that enables bidirectional photocatalytic interconversion between NAD+ and NADH under red visible light irradiation, achieving 77.0% yield for NADH regeneration and nearly quantitative conversion in NADH…

title: Pepti-DrugPhAI: Multimodal AI-evaluator for functional pharmacokinetics and toxicity of peptides
abstract: Peptide drugs exhibit exceptional selectivity for biological targets and high functional activity making them among the most promising therapeutic agents. However, unsatisfactory pharmacokinetic characteristics remain a critical barrier to their implementation. They often become the primary reason for the failure of promising candidates in preclinical and clinical trials. To address this issue, we present Pepti-DrugPhAI - a comprehensive algorithm for the precise prediction of the pharmacokinetics and toxicity of a wide range of peptide compounds. Unlike many existing solutions, the proposed algorithm is multimodal and can simultaneously process both SMILES representations of chemical structures and amino acid sequences. This ensures efficient processing not only of canonical peptides but also of non-canonical modifications, cyclic structures, and peptide-like small molecules. We also created an original dataset for model training integrating data from public databases and relevant scientific publications. The algorithm simultaneously predicts key parameters including membrane permeability (Caco-2 and PAMPA penetration), distribution and excretion (half-life, clearance, volume of distribution), as well as general and specific toxicity profiles (neurotoxicity, hemolytic activity). A key innovation of the study is the integration of functional pharmacokinetic scoring. The model not only predicts ADMET values but also calculates an adaptive suitability rating for a compound in the context of its specific biological activity. We have conducted a comparative analysis of various data encoding strategies implementing a stack of models ranging from classical machine learning methods to modern transformers and language models in classification modes. Results from testing on independent test sets demonstrate high prediction accuracy and interpretability of features making Pepti-DrugPhAI a powerful tool for more robust selection of promising peptide drug candidates. All data and the code are available in the GitHub repository at https://github.com/EABogdanova/Pepti-DrugPhAI.

title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
abstract: Lead-free halide perovskites based on Ge and Sn avoid the toxicity of Pb, but the two cations favor different structural distortions. The stereochemically active Ge $4s^2$ lone pair drives polar $B$-site off-centering, whereas the larger Sn$^{2+}$ cation favors octahedral tilting. Here, we map how these two instabilities compete across the full composition range of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations with a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential trained on hybrid-functional data. At low temperature the alloy exhibits a morphotropic phase boundary between $x=0.60$ and $0.65$ that separates a ferroelectric monoclinic $Cc$ phase from a monoclinic $P2_1$ phase with mixed antipolar and polar off-centering, with both the tilt pattern and the off-centering order changing discontinuously. The composition-temperature phase diagram reproduces the known transition sequences and temperatures of both end members and reveals an intermediate tetragonal $I4/mcm$ phase near the boundary that has no counterpart in either parent compound. Above the transition temperatures the $B$ cations remain locally off-centered but orientationally disordered. The structural transition at the boundary causes a jump in the band gap at low temperature, whereas at $350$ K the gap decreases smoothly with Sn content. These results establish $B$-site mixing as a means to tune polar and rotational order in lead-free halide perovskites.

title: Hybrid Machine Learning for Physically Consistent Prediction of Mutual Diffusion Coefficients in Binary Liquid Mixtures
abstract: Experimental data on mutual diffusion coefficients in liquid mixtures are scarce, and existing prediction methods are unreliable for non-ideal mixtures. Building on HADES, our hybrid model for self-diffusion coefficients, we introduce the Enhanced Vignes Equation (EVE), which augments the Vignes equation with a deep-set model. Its inputs are molecular descriptors derived from SMILES and activity-coefficient information from HANNA, a machine-learning model for activity coefficients. EVE predicts Maxwell--Stefan diffusion coefficients; the corresponding Fickian coefficients follow from the thermodynamic factor, likewise obtained from HANNA. Trained and evaluated on 2106 experimental data points for 123 binary mixtures, EVE outperforms all available semi-empirical models, halving the mean absolute relative error for mixtures without experimental infinite-dilution diffusion data. Combined with HADES, EVE yields the complete set of self- and mutual diffusion coefficients of a binary mixture from SMILES and pure-component viscosities alone. EVE and HADES are available at https://ml-prop.mv.rptu.de/, and the code is fully disclosed.

title: Crystal Nucleation Driven by Microjets from Hydrodynamically Interacting Thermocavitation Bubbles
abstract: Primary nucleation predominantly dictates the physicochemical, optical and mechanical properties of crystals emerging from solution. Here, we reveal a previously unrecognized nucleation mechanism arising from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions using laser-induced thermocavitation bubble pairs. Under confinement, antiphase generation of two bubbles produces a micron-scale, high-speed liquid jet. Upon impact with the surrounding supersaturated liquid, this microjet generates intense localized shear, thereby inducing crystallization of the model inorganic salt, potassium permanganate. Under identical laser energies and supersaturation levels, crystallization was not observed in single-bubble experiments, in which no microjet was present. We show that the crystallization probability increases with microjet velocity. Boundary integral simulations reveal how experimental parameters such as confinement, bubble spacing, and laser energy govern microjet formation and velocity. We quantify the relationship between jet velocity and the observed enhancement in crystal nucleation kinetics by incorporating shear into the kinetic prefactor in classical nucleation theory. By combining experiments, theory, and simulations, we establish how microjets emerging from bubble-bubble hydrodynamic interactions may influence crystallization kinetics, opening new opportunities for the manufacture of crystalline materials.

title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
abstract: The function of oxide materials, from solid-oxide fuel cells to solar thermochemical fuel production, depends on their oxygen vacancies. Their formation energetics have been mapped systematically for ternary perovskites, but reported values for the binary oxides, their conceptual and thermochemical building blocks, remain scattered across studies with differing computational methods. Here we report a systematic r$^2$SCAN density functional theory survey of neutral oxygen vacancy formation energies across 39 binary main-group metal oxide polymorphs spanning groups 1, 2, 13, 14, and 15, using the ShakeNBreak method to locate reconstructed defect ground states. The formation energies span 8 eV and decrease down each group and, for most multivalent cations, with increasing oxidation state. Both trends follow the reducibility of the cation. An interpretable crystal feature model is fit to these energies; its inputs are properties of the pristine bulk, with the reduction potential alternatively taken from tabulated thermochemistry. Retaining only its two dominant descriptors, the crystal reduction potential and the band gap, the model reproduces the formation energies with a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV, lower than that of its four-descriptor parent model for transition-metal perovskites. The bond-breaking and stability terms of the full Born-Haber fit prove statistically null for the binary oxides, and the largest residuals identify the hosts where electron accommodation departs from the cation-reduction picture that the descriptors encode. The dataset provides a benchmark for machine-learning interatomic potentials, and the model estimates vacancy formation energies of main-group oxides from bulk properties alone.

title: Automated classification of Echinococcus multilocularis protoscolex viability using machine learning for high-throughput drug screening.
abstract: Alveolar echinococcosis, caused by the parasite Echinococcus multilocularis, is a potentially lethal disease that requires the development of new medical treatments. Current drug screening methods depend on manual microscopy to count stained and unstained protoscoleces to determine viability, a process that is often slow and subject to human error. This study developed machine learning models to automate the classification of protoscolex survival to accelerate drug discovery. A total of 111 images containing 1,302 protoscoleces stained with eosin or methylene blue were analyzed.

title: Halogen Fluorine Unlocks Ru Activity for Olefins Production from Syngas
abstract: Olefins production from syngas via Fischer–Tropsch synthesis requires catalysts that favor olefins formation, maintain intrinsic activity, and suppress CO2 and CH4 formation. Sodium-promoted ruthenium nanoparticles shift the product distribution toward α-olefins but suppress Ru activity by more than 90%, necessitating higher Ru loadings. We show that incorporating inorganic fluorine into Na-promoted Ru catalysts increases activity 2.5-fold while maintaining 72.1% α-olefins selectivity and ∼5.0% combined selectivity to CO2 and CH4.

title: Reprogramming tumor network resilience: chemical biology, nanomedicine, and intelligent oncology for clinical translation
abstract: BackgroundThe dynamic interactions between the signaling networks, the intracellular organelles and the tumor microenvironment (TME) are increasingly recognized to be a systems-level phenomenon in the development of resistance to cancer. Individual molecule and pathway levels signaling, rewiring have failed to cure the clinical disease with compensatory measures.PurposeThis review proposes an integrated framework for understanding cancer as a network-mediated disease, shaped by intra-organelle communication and microenvironmental cues, and examines how this systems-level view can inform the…

title: Competing lattice instabilities in epitaxially strained BaSnO3
abstract: We use density functional theory to map the lattice-dynamical landscape of BaSnO3 under biaxial compressive strain and uncover the hierarchy of structural instabilities. Our results demonstrate that the phase stability of strained BaSnO3 cannot be inferred from the softening of the polar mode alone. Instead it is governed by the competition among lattice instabilities and their anharmonic coupling to structural relaxation. Two-mode energy-surface analyses show that the polar and rotational order parameters interact predominantly competitively. While A- and M-point octahedral rotations become unstable before the zone-center polar mode and dominate the harmonic response for moderate values of strain, they are related to a continuous transition without anharmonic lattice coupling and a moderate gain of energy with strain. Large strain may induce a first order transition to a supertetragonal polar state. Once this state is stabilized, the magnitude of polarization and ferroelectric energy well depth are comparable to BaTiO3 under compressive strain. Furthermore, we discuss how an electric field or electron doping may tip the balance between the different modes and favor of the supertetragonal structure over antipolar and rotational alternatives at a reduced critical strain.

title: Filling and Sealing Carbon Nanotubes by Local Anodic Oxidation
abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are prime nanofluidic conduits and nanopores for studying matter under extreme confinement. Since most synthesis routes yield CNTs with closed ends, opening and filling strategies are required to access their interior for fluid and ion transport, whereas studies of the encapsulated species themselves may additionally require sealing to prevent their escape in dry or vacuum environments. Capacitively coupled local anodic oxidation (LAO) in an atomic force microscope (AFM) has been shown to cut individual CNTs at predefined positions, but whether cutting induces opening, filling, or sealing has remained unclear. Using spatially resolved micro-Raman spectroscopy, we find that LAO cutting surprisingly produces filled CNT segments that remain sealed under dry Ar atmosphere for weeks. The magnitudes of the blueshift and broadening of the innermost-wall radial breathing-like mode are consistent with water filling, pointing to the water meniscus condensed between the AFM tip and the substrate as the source of CNT filling during cutting. High-vacuum annealing at 140 °C releases the encapsulated species from some, but not all, segments, indicating a thermally surmountable barrier rather than re-formed end caps. This one-step cut-fill-seal capability offers a route to diameter-resolved studies of nanoconfined water and aqueous solutions, and to zeptoliter-scale sample delivery for vacuum-based analytical techniques.

title: Quantum-logic detection of rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecules
abstract: Collisions between molecules govern chemical reactions and energy transfer across a range of different environments from interstellar space to the Earth's atmosphere. Despite their fundamental importance, molecular collisions have traditionally been studied through ensemble-averaged experiments which obscure the dynamics of individual scattering events on the quantum level. Probing single molecular collisions with quantum-state resolution has thus far remained a major experimental challenge. Here, we demonstrate a method for detecting individual rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecular ions with neutral atoms using quantum-logic techniques. We prepare individual trapped N$_2^+$ ions in their rotational ground state, subject them to a beam of helium atoms and detect isolated collision events through their effects on the motion of the trapped ions. Quantum-logic-spectroscopic measurements reveal changes of the molecular state upon collision enabling the determination of the probability of rotationally inelastic scattering. The experiments are analysed by comparison with quantum and classical scattering calculations yielding detailed insights into the underlying collision dynamics. By combining single-collision detection with non-destructive readout of the molecular quantum state, our approach establishes a new experimental framework for investigating molecular scattering beyond conventional ensemble measurements. It opens a route towards investigating state-to-state scattering in individual molecules and exploring molecular interactions at the level of single quantum-state resolved events.

title: Potential for helicity-mediated reverse intersystem crossing in boron--nitrogen-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons with inverted singlet-triplet gaps
abstract: The prospect of exothermic reverse intersystem crossing (rISC) in organic chromophores with inverted singlet-triplet (INVEST) excited states has stimulated considerable interest in next-generation emitters. However, realizing efficient spin conversion remains challenging because energetic inversion does not necessarily imply the appreciable spin-orbit coupling (SOC) required for rISC. Here, we investigate direct ${\rm S}_1-{\rm T}_1$ SOC in 85 INVEST candidates comprising 32 azaphenalenes, 7 non-alternant hydrocarbons, and 46 boron-nitrogen-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (BNPAHs), all previously predicted to exhibit negative singlet-triplet gaps using a correlated wavefunction method at reliably optimized molecular geometries. While the azaphenalenes and non-alternant hydrocarbons exhibit negligible direct SOC, 28 of the 46 BNPAHs display finite coupling. Analysis of molecular geometries and natural transition orbitals suggests that SOC variations depend on molecular topology, orbital orientation, and electronic-state symmetry rather than nonplanarity or excited-state character alone. We estimate direct-rISC rates with a Marcus model, identifying selected BNPAHs with rates approaching $10^7\,{\rm s}^{-1}$.

title: Deep Learning-Enabled Magnetic Bead-Capture Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization Enables Multiplex Identification and Digital Counting of Pathogenic Bacteria.
abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are among the most prevalent infectious diseases worldwide. For complicated and antimicrobial-resistant cases, timely diagnosis is critical for guiding targeted therapy and improving patient outcomes. While conventional urine culture suffers from prolonged turnaround times and low positive detection rates, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) has emerged as a rapid, highly specific alternative.

title: Rhδ+ Anchored on Rh–Fe Bimetallic Nano-islands Ensures Highly Efficient CO Hydrogenation to Ethanol
abstract: The direct synthesis of ethanol from syngas faces a key challenge: achieving high selectivity at high CO conversion while elucidating the catalytic reaction mechanism. Here, we develop a catalyst comprising highly dispersed Rh–Fe bimetallic nano-islands supported on mixed-phase TiO2, which overcomes the trade-off between catalytic activity and ethanol selectivity, achieving an ethanol selectivity of 62.5% among all carbon-containing products at a CO conversion of 55.8%. Meanwhile, CO2 selectivity is greatly reduced to 8.1%.

title: Programmable amide bond formation using de novo ligases
abstract: Amide bond formation is of central importance in the chemical industry, underpinning the synthesis of small bioactive molecules, macrocycles, peptides and their conjugates. Conventional methods of amide synthesis rely on stoichiometric coupling agents and costly protecting group manipulations. While biocatalysis can alleviate some of these challenges, enzymes typically operate across a narrow range of substrates and their adaptation to new coupling partners requires extensive engineering. Here we show that de novo amide ligases featuring a cysteine catalytic triad can be programmed computationally to operate across diverse substrate classes with high selectivity. We first designed complementary peptide ligases to selectively functionalise either the N-terminus or a single lysine residue of a polypeptide sequence containing 36 competing lysines. Crystal structures of both ligases show excellent agreement with the designs, with structural modelling suggesting that amidation outcompetes hydrolysis because the catalytically competent geometry forms only upon acceptor binding. We then extended our approach to the synthesis of small bioactive molecules by designing stereoselective ligases that mediate a key amide bonding forming step in the synthesis of the preventative HIV therapeutic lenacapavir. These results establish de novo enzyme design as a programmable platform for achieving selective amide bond formations across a wide range of molecular targets.

title: Beyond Small Molecules: Computational and AI-Assisted Protein and Peptide Engineering Against the SARS-CoV-2 Nsp12–Nsp7–Nsp8 Replication Complex
abstract: Antiviral development against SARS-CoV-2 has focused largely on small-molecule inhibitors of the main protease and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and on antibodies targeting spike. Antigenic evolution has reduced the activity of many spike-directed antibodies, while resistance-associated substitutions have been identified for enzyme inhibitors. The nsp12–nsp7–nsp8 replication complex offers a complementary target: its subunit interfaces support assembly and processive RNA synthesis and may be accessible to engineered proteins and peptides.

title: De novo design of ligases for programmable site-specific protein ubiquitylation
abstract: Protein ubiquitylation regulates numerous cellular processes, but difficulties in generating site-specifically ubiquitylated proteins limit our understanding of individual modification events. In cells, ubiquitylation is mediated by an E1-E2-E3 enzyme cascade, with substrate recognition largely determined by more than 600 human E3 ligases, making it challenging to redirect ubiquitin transfer to a chosen lysine. Here we use RFdiffusion3 to design ubiquitin ligases from scratch that use a cysteine-based catalytic triad to conjugate an activated ubiquitin donor to a selected lysine in a chosen target substrate. Of 48 tested designs, 35 ubiquitylated a model peptide, with the most active ligases achieving near-quantitative ubiquitin transfer. We next challenged the approach with the homotrimeric sliding clamp proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), whose ubiquitylation at lysine (K) 164 governs DNA damage tolerance while displaying 45 off-target lysines for ubiquitination. Screening of 48 designs delivered a site-selective ligase. Incorporation of a single activity-increasing substitution and coupling to E1-dependent donor activation resulted in 90% conversion from unactivated ubiquitin, delivering higher rates and superior selectivity compared to a natural promiscuous E2. Using this cascade, we transferred di-, tri- and tetraubiquitin chains of defined length to PCNA K164 through a native isopeptide bond. These results establish de novo enzyme design as a route towards programmable, site-specific protein ubiquitylation. That a single de novo designed protein can bind both an activated ubiquitin donor and a globular target, and use a proficient catalytic machinery to selectively transfer ubiquitin to one lysine among 45, illustrates the level of functional complexity now within reach of de novo enzyme design.

title: Defect Topology Governs the Optical Response of Doped Amorphous Silicon
abstract: The influence of defect topology and chemical doping on the optical response of amorphous silicon (a-Si) remains unresolved. In this study, hybrid-functional density functional theory and linear-response calculations are employed to examine four structurally distinct continuous random networks with substitutional boron and phosphorus doping. The calculated optical properties reproduce key experimental trends and demonstrate that dopant sensitivity is determined not only by defect concentration, but also by the character and spatial organization of defects. A configuration with fully extended 4-fold coordination shows the strongest dielectric perturbation to doping, while dopant effects in networks with pre-existing defect states are more varied. For most networks, the dielectric response is more strongly perturbed by boron than phosphorus. Notably, a network having both 3- and 5-fold defects with a total defect fraction of 7.4% reverses the typical boron-dominant response of other cases, becoming more sensitive to phosphorus. Tauc and optical sum-rule analyses further indicate that network topology defines the broader optical landscape, whereas doping primarily affects states near the gap and redistributes spectral weight. These findings establish defect topology as a microscopic control parameter that links amorphous structure, dopant activity, and optical response in amorphous silicon.

title: DETER: Suppression During Pretraining for Tamper Resistance
abstract: Open-weight language models can acquire knowledge that could enable biological, chemical, or cyber misuse. Any attempt to limit such knowledge must remain effective after the model weights are released and can be fine-tuned. Unlearning applied after pretraining can be rapidly undone, whereas filtering the pretraining corpus offers greater resistance. We ask whether actively suppressing knowledge during pretraining can further increase the fine-tuning required to acquire it. Even simple gradient ascent interleaved with standard pretraining on the filtered corpus makes medical knowledge harder to acquire through adversarial fine-tuning than filtering alone or post-hoc unlearning. At 1B parameters, reaching the held-out PubMed loss of an unfiltered model requires over 20$\times$ as many PubMed fine-tuning tokens as after filtering alone. Retained knowledge is evaluated using both held-out data and downstream tasks. Across model sizes, varying suppression strength reveals an increasingly favorable trade-off between fine-tuning difficulty and held-out loss on retained pretraining data. These results point to pretraining as an effective stage for making unwanted capabilities harder to acquire through subsequent fine-tuning. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/MEGlr/DETER}{\texttt{github.com/MEGlr/DETER}}.

title: The infrared vacuum reduces the laser energy needed to break molecular bonds of simple molecules
abstract: Vibrational strong coupling within a few molecules has recently been demonstrated in infrared nanocavities at room temperature, opening new alternatives to explore chemical reactions assisted by the confined electromagnetic vacuum. However, the intrinsic mechanisms of how the quantized electromagnetic mode modifies reactivity are not fully understood. We study infrared photodissociation of a single molecule strongly coupled to a resonant infrared nanocavity mode. The coupled system is driven by a monochromatic infrared laser that vibrationally excites the molecule directly or injects photons into the nanocavity field. We compare the intracavity dynamics of CO2 and H2O molecules and demonstrate that the driving energy required for dissociation is up to three orders of magnitude lower inside the cavity by injecting photons into the nanocavity than by driving the molecule directly. We show that photodissociation enhancements are due to the interplay between nuclear anharmonicity, stronglight-mattercoupling, and vacuum field polarisation according to the dipolar nature of the molecular bond. Our results provide the conceptual and numerical tools for understanding how to control chemical processes and to design nanophotonics experiments at the few-molecule level within a cavity quantum electrodynamics perspective.

title: Materials research with a general-purpose agent
abstract: Over the last decade we have built Alexandria, an open database of about 15 million density-functional calculations of crystals. It includes PBE, PBEsol, SCAN and TB-mBJ results, structures relaxed at pressures up to 150 GPa, dielectric tensors and about 145,000 electron-phonon calculations, together with more than 400 million structures relaxed with machine-learned potentials. On these data we trained a generative model for crystal structures, a universal interatomic potential and graph neural networks for more than ten properties, from band gaps to superconducting critical temperatures. From the convex hull we computed a reaction graph of the 17.4 billion reactions between its 193,416 stable compounds. Here we give all of this to a general-purpose language-model agent. Working unattended, the agent screens the database for a solar absorber, drops a candidate whose synthesis releases too little energy, and writes a synthesis plan with precursors, crucible and atmosphere. Asked about the well-studied Ba-Zr-S system, it finds an unreported sulfide and designs the experiment that would confirm or rule it out. Asked for an air-stable alternative, it designs one and tests it against new structures from the generative model. With web search alone, the same agent proposes what the literature already discusses. Put together, the data, the models and the reaction graph let a general agent do what none of them does alone: go from a question in plain words to an experiment that a laboratory can run and test.

title: Symmetry-Enabled Ferroelectric Valley Transduction in Rhombohedral Bilayer WSe$_2$
abstract: Ferroelectric polarization couples to the layer degree of freedom in a bilayer, but a valley-selective energy response requires the valleys to carry different interlayer character. Rhombohedral bilayer WSe$_2$ meets that condition by symmetry: three-fold rotation forbids interlayer tunneling at the $K$ valley, while strong hybridization remains at $Γ$. The resulting contrast converts the band-effective ferroelectric layer asymmetry into a shift of the $K$ edge, and so displaces the $K$--$Γ$ landscape: a finite-field fit that does not impose the rule leaves the $K$ coupling consistent with zero, and the shift reaches \polshiftdft~meV, the most that asymmetry can give a single valley. Reversing the polarization mirrors the valley landscape in displacement field, so the two registries have equal and opposite differential transconductance $g_d$ at zero field. In the ideal symmetric limit a second parity holds about each registry's own compensation field and places a zero of $g_d$ there. The valley-dependent screening calculated here displaces that zero by only \gdnulllow\% at the read point, so device asymmetry limits the accuracy. The result links a known stacking selection rule to ferroelectric valley transduction, with a quantitative valley shift and a directly testable transport signature.

title: Surface Evaporation Protocol for Solution-Processed Bulk-Heterojunction Films via Coarse-Grained Simulations
abstract: We present a coarse-grained molecular dynamics protocol for simulating solvent evaporation applied to P3HT:PCBM bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) films. Prior reported protocols lacked an explicit air–film interface or resorted to monatomic solvents with heavily coarse-grained solute models to work. Our approach maintains an explicit air–film interface, handles polyatomic solvents, and is better suited for complex molecular models.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Evidential Deep Regression for Universal Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian Models
abstract: Universal density functional theory (DFT) Hamiltonian models trained across broad chemical and structural spaces offer an efficient route from atomic structure to electronic properties. However, estimating prediction uncertainty alongside fast Hamiltonian predictions remains a challenge. In this work, we present EviDTB, an evidential deep regression approach for tight-binding DFT Hamiltonians that effectively estimates prediction uncertainty in a single forward pass. Compared with deep ensembles, Monte Carlo dropout, and mean-variance estimation (MVE), EviDTB achieves a better balance between computational cost and uncertainty-quantification performance. On 5,478 held-out test structures, EviDTB achieves a full spin--orbit-coupled (SOC) Hamiltonian matrix-element mean absolute error of 0.622meV. Its mean uncertainty per atom correlates with the mean local squared prediction error (Spearman $ρ=0.812$); removing the 15% most uncertain structures reduces the 99th percentile of this error by 78%, from 16.63 to 3.72eV$^2$. This score offers a practical way to prioritize candidates for first-principles verification. We hope that combining fast Hamiltonian prediction with uncertainty-guided screening will accelerate the search for materials with desirable electronic properties.

title: Zero-Field Optical Readout of Quintet States in Through-Space Coupled Tetracene Oligomers at Room Temperature
abstract: Optically addressable electron spins are promising platforms for quantum technologies, with molecular systems offering chemical control over their spin and optical properties. Achieving optical readout of molecular spin states at room temperature and without an applied magnetic field is an important step towards their practical implementation. Quintet states generated via singlet fission are promising optically addressable multilevel qudits, but their intrinsic spin transitions at zero and weak magnetic fields remain largely unexplored, while substantial room-temperature quintet coherence has predominantly been demonstrated in structurally constrained molecular architectures. Here, we combine zero-field optically detected magnetic resonance (zero-field ODMR) with transient and pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) to investigate the magnetic-field dependence and coherent spin properties of quintet states in conformationally flexible, through-space coupled tetracene oligomers. We demonstrate zero-field optical readout of quintet states at room temperature in both tetracene dimers and hexamers, and map the response of optically detected transitions to weak applied magnetic fields. Complementary EPR measurements support quintet formation through stochastic exchange fluctuations and demonstrate a room-temperature phase-memory time of 446 ns, showing that the conformational dynamics enabling high-spin formation remain compatible with substantial spin coherence. Together, these results integrate field-free optical readout, weak-field response and room-temperature spin coherence within a chemically modular, through-space coupled molecular architecture, expanding the design space for optically addressable molecular qudits and quantum sensors.

title: A Hierarchical Harmonic-to-Anharmonic Framework for ab initio Screening and Mechanistic Analysis of Negative Thermal Expansion in ZrV2O7
abstract: Negative thermal expansion (NTE) in framework materials arises from complex lattice dynamics that are challenging to capture using conventional theoretical approaches. Here, we establish a hierarchical computational strategy for investigating NTE in ZrV2O7, integrating the quasiharmonic approximation (QHA), temperature-dependent effective potentials (TDEP), and machine-learning-accelerated ab initio molecular dynamics (ML-MD). Quasi-harmonic lattice-dynamical calculations identify low-frequency phonon modes with negative Grüneisen parameters as inexpensive screening descriptors, while TDEP incorporates finite-temperature anharmonicity and ML-MD further reveals temperature-dependent structural distortions that drive the lattice contraction. The observations are further corroborated with X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements. The concurrent increase in transverse displacement (uT) provides microscopic evidence for a quasi-rigid-unit-mode (QRUM) mechanism underlying the NTE behaviour at elevated temperatures. This is consistent with previous reports on other framework materials, including ZrW2O7, where collective polyhedral rotations and transverse atomic motions have been linked to NTE. Overall, our results demonstrate how relatively inexpensive lattice-dynamical descriptors can identify potential NTE materials, while higher-level anharmonic simulations can then resolve the underlying structural mechanisms at the atomic scale.

title: Chiral-phonon-induced anomalous Hall effect in bilayer MoSe$_2$
abstract: We demonstrate that optically driven chiral phonons induce an anomalous Hall response in a nonmagnetic, centrosymmetric material. Using first-principles calculations to parameterize an effective $\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{p}$ Hamiltonian for bilayer MoSe$_2$, we show that circular excitation of an $E_u$ phonon generates a circular dynamical Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The resulting Floquet bands carry same-sign Berry curvature at the two valleys, producing a Hall response whose sign follows the phonon handedness. We obtain a range of $σ_{xy}\sim10^{-2}-0.21$ $\frac{e^2}{2π\hbar}$ for experimentally accessible light pulses. Our results show that chiral phonons provide a route to controlling electronic Berry curvature and transport on ultrafast time scales.

title: PDO Drug Screening Data for Evaluating and Training AI Drug Response Prediction Models
abstract: Anti-cancer drug response prediction (DRP) is critically important for precision oncology and therapeutic development. Currently, most DRP models are developed using drug screening data from immortalized cancer cell lines, which can differ substantially from patient tumors at the genomic and molecular levels, even though patient tumor response is the ultimate prediction target. To help bridge this gap and bring DRP models closer to their intended clinical application, we conducted four drug screening studies using patient-derived organoids (PDOs), which more faithfully recapitulate patient tumors than immortalized cell lines. These studies generated data for improving and evaluating DRP models, including multi-omics profiles of PDO lines, drug feature data, and treatment response measurements. Using these data, we retrained and evaluated multiple publicly available DRP models under three model-building scenarios: training models using cell line data only, training models using combined cell line and PDO data, and pretraining models on cell line data followed by fine-tuning on PDO data. We then evaluated and compared model prediction performance on PDOs across these analysis scenarios. In addition, we also assessed the consistency of drug screening viability data generated by different laboratories using different assay technologies and/or experimental protocols.

title: Intense and stable second-harmonic generation in robust MePEA-based quasi-2D halide perovskite crystals
abstract: Quasi-2D halide perovskites offer a unique platform for nonlinear optics applications, where structural and optical properties are tuned by the variation of organic spacer cations. Notably, quasi-2D perovskite single crystals can demonstrate intense and stable second-harmonic generation signals when a proper composition is selected. Here, the influence of phenethylammonium and 4-methyl-2-phenylethylammonium spacers on the crystal symmetry and second-harmonic signal response of quasi-2D perovskite phases with a varying number of single-octahedron [PbX$_6$]$^{4-}$ layers ($n$) is investigated. High-quality perovskite crystals with lateral dimensions of several hundred micrometers are fabricated using a cavity-confined crystallization synthesis method. Optical characterization of the crystals shows strong and temporally stable second-harmonic generation. Power-dependent and polarization-resolved measurements confirm the second-order nonlinear origin of the observed response and reveal anisotropic emission patterns. Our results demonstrate a direct correlation between spacer-induced center-symmetry breaking and nonlinear optical activity. These results establish quasi-2D halide perovskites as a promising class of symmetry-engineered materials for efficient frequency conversion and integrated nonlinear photonics.

title: Buffer-Gas-Assisted Fluorescence Spectroscopy of Molecular Ions
abstract: Sustained fluorescence detection of generic molecules has been challenging due to the lack of cycling transitions and limited photon budgets. We demonstrate a nondestructive method for continuous fluorescence of strongly rovibronically open molecular ions, $^{232}$ThF$^+$. Effective quasi-cycling transitions are established by room-temperature buffer-gas collisions, which replenish the population back to the laser-addressed states. In situ images and rotationally resolved spectra are obtained without optical repumping or auxiliary atomic readout ions. Combined with low-background spectroscopic detection, this approach achieves a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 6 in a 1 s exposure on the P(1) line of $^{232}$ThF$^+$, despite a thermal population of only approximately 0.17% in the addressed state at room temperature. The ability to repeatedly interrogate trapped ions is particularly promising for scarce molecular samples, broadband spectroscopic searches, and in situ monitoring of molecular reactions.

title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses reveal ferro-aging-related molecular characteristics and immunological heterogeneity in renal cell carcinoma
abstract: ObjectiveFerro-aging, characterized by chronic iron-dependent oxidative damage and age-related transcriptional alterations, may contribute to the heterogeneity of renal cell carcinoma (RCC). This study aimed to identify ferro-aging-related candidate core genes and evaluate their diagnostic value and biological relevance in RCC.MethodsGSE40435 and GSE66272 were integrated as the training cohort, and GSE53757 was used for external validation. Ferro-aging-related candidate genes were identified by differential expression and machine-learning analyses to construct a diagnostic model. Their biological relevance was investigated using immune, molecular subtype, WGCNA, single-cell, and virtual knockout analyses, followed by experimental validation of gene expression and LOX function.ResultsA total of 26 ferro-aging-related differentially expressed genes were identified, from which five candidate core genes-DPEP1, LCN2, LOX, NOX4, and TLR4-were selected. The five-gene diagnostic model showed strong discriminatory performance, with AUCs of 0.952 and 0.978 in the training and independent validation cohorts, respectively. These genes were associated with immune-related and molecular features and exhibited heterogeneous cell-type-resolved expression patterns, with the combined five-gene signature showing relatively higher module scores in the epithelial/tumor epithelial compartment. Virtual knockout identified NNMT and FAM134B as potential common response nodes. LOX knockdown significantly inhibited RCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion and increased lipid peroxidation.ConclusionDPEP1, LCN2, LOX, NOX4, and TLR4 represent potential ferro-aging-related diagnostic biomarkers in RCC. LOX may be associated with RCC progression and ferro-aging-related lipid peroxidation, although the underlying mechanisms require further investigation.

title: Evaluating MSA-Derived Evolutionary Information in Enzyme Recommendation for Biocatalytic Reactions
abstract: Reaction-conditioned enzyme recommendation ranks candidate enzymes for a query chemical transformation, but the contribution of explicit evolutionary context to this task remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we present an exploratory evaluation of multiple sequence alignment (MSA)-derived evolutionary features, integrating full-sequence and pocket-level MSA Transformer representations into EnzymeCage and a benchmark-adapted Horizyn implementation through concatenation or gated fusion.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: SPINKS (Spin Inversion Kinetics Suite): A Fully Automated Python–ORCA Framework for End-to-End Computation of Spin-Crossing Probabilities, Microcanonical, and Canonical Reaction Rate Constants
abstract: We present SPINKS (Spin Inversion Kinetics Suite), a freely available, fully automated Python–ORCA computational framework for an end-to-end evaluation of spin-forbidden reaction kinetics directly from an initial molecular geometry. SPINKS automatically generates, executes, monitors, and processes the ORCA electronic-structure calculations required to determine the minimum-energy crossing point (MECP) between two potential-energy surfaces. It then extracts the spin–orbit coupling (SOC), energy gradients, and Hessians required to construct the reaction coordinate and subsequently evaluates the reduced mass, crossing velocity, and vibrational and rovibrational densities of states. These quantities are used to calculate Landau–Zener and weak coupling spin-crossing probabilities and the corresponding microcanonical and canonical reaction rate constants within the framework of nonadiabatic statistical theory. The workflow automatically generates graphical visualizations and comprehensive text-based outputs while permitting user customization of ORCA input files throughout the calculation. SPINKS shows excellent agreement during validation tests against the independently developed Nonadiabatic Statistical Theory (NAST) package. The NAST program requires manual preparation and transfer of electronic-structure quantities, whereas SPINKS integrates ORCA-based electronic-structure calculations with nonadiabatic dynamics and kinetic calculations within a single end-to-end automated workflow. SPINKS is freely distributed and operates within an accessible software ecosystem based on the free and open-source Python language and the ORCA quantum-chemistry package, which is freely available for academic use. The SPINKS framework provides a practical, reproducible, and extensible platform for routine investigation of spin-forbidden chemical reactions.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Fluorescence Kinetic Fingerprinting of Seven Nucleotides with a Single Eu(III)-Functionalized HOF
abstract: Reliable discrimination of structurally similar nucleotides remains challenging in fluorescence sensing because their shared molecular frameworks often result in overlapping fluorescence responses. Here, a Eu(III)-functionalized hydrogen-bonded organic framework (Eu@MA-BPDC) was used as a single cross-reactive sensing unit to generate multidimensional kinetic fluorescence fingerprints for discriminating seven nucleotides: ATP, ADP, AMP, GTP, CTP, UTP, and GMP.

title: Towards automated development of real fuel combustion models: from quantum chemistry to chemical kinetics
abstract: The development of predictive chemical kinetic models for real fuel combustion requires the integration of accurate quantum chemistry methods, statistical dynamical rate theories, thermochemical property estimation, and systematic mechanism construction. In this perspective, we discuss the current state of this pipeline as applied to combustion chemistry, from wave function and density functional theory methods for the characterization of potential energy surfaces, through transition state theory, its variational and multi-structural extensions, and master equation approaches for…
